## [1.91.284.0] - 2026-10-27

**Five small takes from tstack, in gstack's words.** Theo Browne's tstack (MIT, 2026-10-24) is nine short PR-landing skills; its best ideas that gstack lacked were a verb for an aging pull request, a Codex picker that says what each skill is for, a written grant for unattended sessions, a repo-level rule for porting a contributor's PR, and a visible author line on agent-posted comments. Each lands here as gstack prose and gstack code; no sentence is copied (NOTICE.md). Approved by Garry, 2026-10-26: "Do it, send" (yes to the opt-in attribution callout, off by default).

### Added
- **`/modernize`**: bring an aging pull request onto its current base and decide whether it should still exist. The skill reads the PR as a claim (the problem, the change, what must be true of the codebase), reads its title, body and comments only through `gstack-issue-guard`, reads what moved under it for conflicts in meaning as well as in text, and writes one of three verdicts before anything is pushed: **MODERNIZE** (rebase with the author's commits kept as theirs, `git range-diff` with a one-line reason per changed hunk, the repo's own tests, then `git push --force-with-lease=<branch>:<observed head sha>`), **REWORK** (the problem stands, this diff does not; nothing pushed) or **CLOSE** (recommended with the superseding commit; the PR stays open until someone with the authority says so). The skill never closes a PR and never uses a bare `--force`; `/careful` already rates the lease push MEDIUM. Rows in README, AGENTS.md, `docs/skills.md` (with a deep dive), `docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md`, the root router and `gstack/llms.txt`.
- **Per-skill Codex default prompts**: a template's `codex_default_prompt:` frontmatter key becomes that skill's `default_prompt` in `agents/openai.yaml`, the sentence Codex's picker inserts when a user chooses the skill; a template without the key keeps `Use <name> for this task.`. `/ship`, `/review`, `/qa`, `/autoplan`, `/office-hours`, `/land-and-deploy` and `/modernize` carry one. The key is generator input only. No host's SKILL.md render carries it (Claude strips it; the allowlist hosts never copy it), so every pinned render is byte-identical. `bin/gstack-host-renders.sh`'s proof that a yaml file is gstack's accepts any `default_prompt` line.
- **`gstack-post --attribute "<model> on behalf of <login>"`** on `pr-comment`, `issue-comment` and `reply`: opt-in and off by default, it opens the comment with a `> [!NOTE]` callout (`🤖 **<text>**`) naming who wrote it, then the body as written. The callout bytes are scanned and bound into the MEDIUM confirmation token with the body, so a changed attribution needs a new token (findings are reported at the body file's own line numbers, a finding in the callout as `PART: attribute`); the flag is refused (exit 64) on a PR body, a title or an issue body, and for empty, multi-line or over-200-character text. `review/greptile-triage.md` says when to add it to a reply.
- **`docs/unattended.md` "What an unattended session may do"**: merge never (nor auto-merge, a merge queue or `gh pr ready` on a PR the run did not open); force-push only the run's own branch, after a rebase the plan or a `/modernize` disposition named, with `git range-diff` in the handoff and a lease pinned to the observed sha; tests only by the methods the repository's instructions name, no ask-first; proof is what the run observed itself. Anything outside the list is a pending approval item. `/ship`'s handoff section points at it (one line in the lazy section; this PR adds no skeleton bytes).
- **CONTRIBUTING.md "Porting a contributor's PR"**: review and test the port head first (a fork's green checks prove nothing here), keep their commits as theirs with `Co-authored-by` on anything rewritten, your fixes on top as separate commits, the port names the original and its author, and the original closes with a specific thank-you linking the port; closing without landing is a maintainer's call. The repo-side home of the crew rule in `docs/captain.md`.

### Tests
- `test/modernize-skill.test.ts` (new): the verdict table and its order before any push, the never-close rule, the range-diff and pinned-lease lines, the `/careful` MEDIUM rating, and every catalog row a new skill owes.
- `test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts`: the seven prompts reach `openai.yaml`, a skill without the key keeps the fallback, `extractCodexDefaultPrompt` reads quoted and plain values inside the frontmatter only, and no host render carries the key.
- `test/gstack-post.test.ts`: no flag means the body is sent as written; the callout on all three comment operations and on GitLab; scan and token cover the callout; refusals on the other operations and bad text.

### Gate integrity
- The one threshold this PR moves is the ship union cap in `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts`, 1.7525 → 1.7529 under GStack Minder's grant. On the tree merged with 392f50d4 (v1.91.281.0) the union is 329,024 / 187,706 = 1.7529 against main's 1.7525 (pinned at a measured 1.7524 by #3516), the handoff pointer line being this PR's only ship bytes; the skeleton is main's 60,900 (0 skeleton bytes added). Earlier merges of this PR pinned 1.7405 on top of #3487's 1.7400 (326,691 bytes on the f27a7605 merge) and 1.7528 on top of main's 1.7524 (329,005 bytes on the 1f246e35 merge) the same way. No timeout, trial count or case kind changed. `test/catalog-budget.test.ts` moves 1,314 → 1,359 token-equivalents for the new skill, re-measured on top of main's `/ubicloud` and `/design-motion` rows (pre-addition 5,249 bytes on d9b0d600, modernize adds 178, measured 5,427 = 1,357 on the merged tree; 9 bytes left), and `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` is recaptured on the merged tree, where the hoist moved modernize's preamble into a lazy section (`modernize` 9466 → 3772) and `alwaysOnTotal` goes 7769 → 7880 (capture × 1.05). No pinned render in `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json` changed size.

## [1.91.282.0] - 2026-10-27

**A merge the pre-merge verify accepted no longer freezes the queue, and a slot stamp touches only the stamp files.** Train 24 (2026-10-27) merged #3434 and #3453, then froze on #3453's post-merge check and paid a $31 backstop: the pre-merge verify judged the lane's CHANGELOG as main's plus the pin's own entry and said MERGE_CONDITION, the post-merge check compared main to T2 section by section, and T2's one `[Unreleased]` (both stacked entries) had become two released sections. In both slots `gstack-restamp` also listed `lib/ship-policy.ts` as a fifth stamp file, because the lane's uncommitted base merge made #3511's `DOCS_CAPS_KEY_VERSION` look like the branch's own tentative key. And `mergeChangelogs` refused the stacked child outright, so the lane's hand resolve dropped #3453's two wording fixes to the released 1.91.276.0 entry.

### Fixed
- **`gstack-ship-queue verify --train`** (`lib/ship-queue-train-verify.ts`): one CHANGELOG rule before and after the merge. Post-merge, main confirms when its tree is T<i> modulo stamps, or differs from T<i> in the CHANGELOG alone while being its own first parent's CHANGELOG (the main the pre-merge verify saw) plus the PR's own entry, the rule `mergedIn` applied pre-merge; the `main:` line says "except CHANGELOG.md, main <sha12>'s CHANGELOG.md plus #<n>'s own entry". The own lines are the pin's authored CHANGELOG lines or the lines `mergeChangelogs` writes for that pin against main, so a tool-written correction bullet passes. A freeze lists a slot GitHub reports MERGED as merged (its reason says "merged on GitHub without a verified tree"), never under `unmerged`, so the rebuild after the repair does not seat it again; the record is built from the one GitHub read that decided to freeze, so a slot that read MERGED stays merged when GitHub stops answering a moment later, and a slot unreadable beside a merged one is left out of `unmerged` and named in the reason ("unreadable on GitHub, left out of unmerged; seat it in a train by hand once gh pr view answers"), so the `NEXT:` after the repair omits it; and a first slot GitHub reports MERGED whose squash fails the post-merge check freezes the queue instead of answering "nothing of the train merged" while main already holds the unverified squash; when GitHub's answer for a slot cannot be read, the verify refuses (`QUEUE_PROOF_MISSING`, "whether #<n> merged on GitHub could not be read") and asks to be rerun, never "nothing merged". A main whose CHANGELOG equals its parent's is not "the parent's plus the PR's own entry" (`ownEntryAboveMain`: "no entry of the PR's own above it"), so a squash that lost the entry the gate carried is refused.
- **`gstack-restamp` stamp_paths** (`lib/restamp.ts`): a line the base added since the pin's fork point is the base's, whether the base merge is committed or still staged; `branchAddedLines` leaves it out and the stage detail says "N line(s) the base added since the fork point are the base's, not this branch's, and stay (<file>: N)". #3514's receipt bound (`stampOnlyLine`) refuses such a move after the fact only while the moved version is older than the base's at the build; a key at the base version passes it, so the restamp is the guard. A base diff git cannot run is a refusal ("cannot diff <since>..<base> for the stamp_paths stage"), never an empty "nothing added" set that would move the base's lines again.
- **`mergeChangelogs`** (`lib/changelog-check.ts`): a stacked child whose parent squash-merged and was released since the merge base (`carryReleasedParent`) is a merge, not a hand resolve. The parent's lines leave the child's `[Unreleased]`; each line the child changed inside them becomes `- Correction to the <version> entry below: "<old>" should read "<new>".` (a dropped line "no longer applies", a line added between the parent's "Addition to the <version> entry below") under the child's own `### Gate integrity`, appended to one it already has. The released entry stays main's byte for byte. Without the merge base the shape is GSTA-67's dropped heading and stays null. `mergeChangelogsWithNotes` returns the carried corrections; the slot one-liner in docs/ship-policy.md prints them. `mergeStep` (train build) passes the merge base, so a child of an already-released parent seats; from slot 2 on, where the prefix already holds an earlier slot's `[Unreleased]` and the sections are unioned, the union takes the carried child, so the gated tree never repeats the released parent's text under the child's heading.

### Tests

### Fixed
- **`scripts/ubicloud/ubi-runner.sh`**: the quota wait budget is a countdown of the seconds spent sleeping for room. Usage reads between sleeps do not eat it, the first log line names the whole `UBI_QUOTA_WAIT`, `UBI_QUOTA_WAIT=0` still refuses on the first poll, and the wait still releases when usage drops.

A usage read that takes 1.2 s keeps the printed 2 s budget (origin/main prints 1 s), a 70 s wait sleeps 30 s twice, and the wait releases when the peer VM disappears.

The review army's lead judgment (`scripts/resolvers/review-army.ts`, rendered into both `review-army.md` sections) gains the one-line **On record** ground that applies the table; its other grounds were tightened by the same byte count so the generated review SKILL.md stays at its pins. The floor ("would fail a test, break production, or lose data or secrets") is unchanged.
- **`docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md` Windows free lane**: the command that shows whether one test is in the curated Windows subset and why not, and which list (`KNOWN_WINDOWS_SAFE`, `WINDOWS_PROBE_SAFE`, `KNOWN_WINDOWS_INCOMPATIBLE`) moves it.

### Fixed

A 10-digit national number after a run word, a bare 11-digit number, an E.164 `+` number and `job`, `id`, `workflow` or `attempt` before one still report; a national number written without its `+` right after a run word reads as a run id, the accepted residual of the ruling that a run id is not a phone number (`gstack-post` has read it that way since GSTA-121).

## [1.91.278.0] - 2026-10-27

**The merge train's tooling stops failing the lanes for things the tooling itself could see.** A head whose only conflict with main was the CHANGELOG got its Free Tests through the dispatch route and the paid screen still called it NOT-RUN; the receipt-versus-prose check read the canonical `REVIEW_LOOP` line as a false mismatch; a PR that writes a new `*_KEY_VERSION` constant as a tentative next-minor version (the convention #3511 introduces) could not clear the train's stamp-only receipt; a pooled pin learned that main had moved onto its files only when the train was built; a watcher had no way to leave a stuck non-required check out of its verdict; and a lane that passed the slot call's remaining order to `gstack-restamp` without its own PR got the same stale list back as the fix. Backlog items from GSTA-119, #3485, #3495 and the 2026-10-27 slot calls.

### Fixed
- **`scripts/eval-readiness.ts`** (#3508): readiness accepts a `workflow_dispatch` Free Tests run at the exact head beside GitHub's `pull_request` run, so a head the dispatch route of docs/ship-policy.md tested starts its paid screen. GitHub's `pull_request` run decides whenever one exists (it built the merge ref; a dispatch builds the head alone, so a newer green dispatch never overrides a red `pull_request` run and an extra red or running dispatch never holds a head its `pull_request` CI cleared); the newest dispatched run decides only for a head with none, a red one blocks, and a `push` run still counts for nothing.
- **`lib/ship-receipt-prose.ts`** (#3513): a number that is the value of a `key=` or `key:` pair is that key's claim alone, whatever the whitespace around the separator, so `REVIEW_LOOP: passes=2 blocking_found=1 deferred=0 noted=4 fixed=8 scope=frozen` and `passes: 2 blocking_found: 1` parse as five claims that all match the receipt instead of a `2 blocking_found` claim.
- **Stamp paths under the next-minor key convention** (#3512): the tree receipt (`lib/tree-receipt.ts`), the carry (`lib/ship-receipt.ts` `stampOnlyText`) and the train's tree-modulo-stamps digest (`scripts/train-gate.ts` `stampFreeTree`) accept a stamp_paths line whose stamp-form version moved to the released version whatever it was before, not only when it was the base's version. The receipt keeps the stamp_paths stage's own bounds (`lib/restamp.ts` `stampOnlyLine`): a moved version older than the gated head's is a released key moved by hand, and one of another width (a 3-digit pin in a 4-digit repository) is never a stamp candidate, so both stay `changed`. The digest collapses every stamp-form mention, so a tentative key and a base-version mention on a base-side line digest the same before and after the slot stamp and `train-backstop` finds the record that covers main.
- **`gstack-restamp --expect-order`**: the `QUEUE_STALE` refusal prints the corrected command instead of the stale list: this PR first when the list left it out (with the message saying every entry read as a predecessor), PRs merged into the local base dropped, an unmerged predecessor kept ahead with a note that it must merge first, and a predecessor GitHub calls merged that the local base does not carry yet kept ahead too, with `fix: git fetch origin <base>` (dropping it would let the recompute, pinned to that local base, allocate the version it already took). The base-moved refusal carries `--pr` too.

### Added
- **`gstack-ship-queue ready` and `train build` read gstack-pr-wait's base-overlap event from git** (handoff GSTA-119; the crew template's sibling trial merge, done by the tool). `ready` prints `BASE_OVERLAP: <base> moved to <sha7> and touches files in this PR: <files>; the train's merge onto <base> is clean` (or the conflicting files) when the base moved onto the PR's files since it forked, and under `--no-screen` a conflict is `QUEUE_TRAIN_CONFLICT` at READY rather than at the train, with the template's fix (report it to the controller; merge the base on its word). A git read that fails prints `conflicts unknown` and refuses nothing. `train build` runs the scratch merges before the fill rule. A seated pin whose files the base moved onto gets `#<pr> BASE_OVERLAP: <base> moved to <sha7> and touches files in this PR: <files>` (the chain's merge onto the pin's own prefix is the verdict), a pin that does not merge is `QUEUE_TRAIN_CONFLICT` while the train is still filling, and a clean pool prints `MERGE_CHECK: T1..T<k> merge clean onto <base>@<sha>` ahead of `QUEUE_TRAIN_WAITING`, so the waiting verdict is also a dry-run merge (#3485).
- **`gstack-pr-wait --exclude <check,...>`** (#3495 follow-up): a named non-required check is left out of the verdict as `gstack-ci-gate --exclude` does, so it neither holds `--until green` while pending nor blocks when it fails; a required check cannot be excluded and the first poll logs the refusal, and while a required-check source cannot be read nothing is excluded (the set may be short), as `gstack-ci-gate` refuses its overrides.

### Tests
- `test/eval-readiness.test.ts`: a dispatched-only head decides green, red and running, a `pull_request` run outranks a dispatched one either way; the runs listing is no longer narrowed to `pull_request`. `test/ship-receipt-prose.test.ts`: the exact `REVIEW_LOOP` line with `passes=2 blocking_found=1` and with `passes=1 blocking_found=0`, the `key: value` spelling with whitespace, plus a real disagreement on the same line. `test/tree-receipt-stamp-sensitive.test.ts`, `test/train-gate.test.ts`, `test/gstack-ship-receipt-docs.test.ts`: a tentative key moved by the restamp is a stamp in the receipt, the digest and the carry; a renamed key, a released key moved by hand or a mention of another width is not. `test/gstack-restamp-queue.test.ts`: the corrected `--expect-order` in each refusal, the own-PR-first lesson and a merged predecessor the local base does not carry. `test/pr-wait.test.ts`: `--exclude` parsing, pending and failed excluded checks, a refused required name, an unreadable required set, and the flag through `prWaitMain`. `test/ship-queue-train-ops.test.ts` and `test/ship-queue-train.test.ts`: the `BASE_OVERLAP:` lines at READY and at build, the `--no-screen` conflict refusal, and `MERGE_CHECK:` beside `QUEUE_TRAIN_WAITING`.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, timeout, trial count or case kind changed. No skill prose changed.

## [1.91.276.0] - 2026-10-27

**Tier 2+ skills load the shared preamble once per session instead of once per invocation.** Every tier 2+ SKILL.md carried the same ~23 KB of preamble (AskUserQuestion format, voice, writing style, completeness, completion protocol and more), so each skill invocation re-read text the conversation already held. That text now renders once per host into `sections/preamble.md` beside each tier 2+ SKILL.md. The SKILL.md keeps a short "Shared preamble (load first)" pointer naming the file and its id (a hash of the shared text before host rewrites), and asks for the Read unless the skill's own earlier Read of that file, headed by that id, is still in context, so other text that merely carries the id cannot stand in for the shared rules. Measured with Anthropic token counting: review's SKILL.md drops from 21,884 to 16,103 tokens, ship from 22,688 to 16,907, office-hours from 27,100 to 23,085 and design-review from 39,040 to 33,261. The shared file is 5,953 tokens, so a skill's first invocation in a session costs about 170 tokens more than before (about 1,900 for office-hours, about 3,800 for plan-eng-review) and every later invocation of that skill saves about 5,800 (4,000 for office-hours, 2,200 for plan-eng-review). The skip is tied to the skill's own copy of the file, so the first invocation of each different skill pays the Read again. A /autoplan run's four review-skill loads carry 17,941 fewer SKILL.md tokens (191,871 → 173,930), and /autoplan and the inline /office-hours loader skip each loaded skill's "Shared preamble (load first)" section, because the parent already holds the shared preamble.

### Changed
- **`scripts/resolvers/preamble-hoist.ts`** (new) renders `{{PREAMBLE}}` for tier 2+ skills: a section moves to the shared file only when this skill's render of it is byte-identical to the shared render, so no skill's instructions change. Sections that name the skill (the start command, Question Tuning, Repo Ownership, Search Before Building, Telemetry), text without its own heading, and skill-specific variants stay inline; a variant that keeps the shared subsection headings carries only its differing `###` subsections. Tier 1 skills keep their short preamble inline. Across all 41 hoisted skills, the SKILL.md with its shared file applied holds exactly the paragraphs the pre-hoist SKILL.md held.
- **`scripts/gen-skill-docs.ts`** emits `sections/preamble.md` per tier 2+ skill and host as a new `preamble` artifact kind, with the same host rewrites, install-root rewrite and runtime preludes as SKILL.md. `setup` already installs every skill's `sections/`, and gstack-built overlay and per-install renders carry the file the same way.
- **`setup --status`**: a bare `sections/<file>` pointer counts as carved only when the skill installs a section other than the shared `preamble.md`, so the new file does not turn on checks for skills that inline their sections on that host.
- **`gstack-doctor --check`**: the `patch` row finds the Codex render's model patch in the review skill's `sections/preamble.md` too, where the hoist moves it; without this the required row failed on every hoisted Codex install.

**The Completeness Principle now asks for complete coverage with minimal code.** Every tier-2+ skill's preamble said "the complete thing is the goal", and ETHOS.md told models to "always prefer A" because "the 70-line delta costs seconds". Models read that as permission to write more code, which is the "50-line job arriving as 400" complaint (GSTA-93). Coverage of the requirement is still non-negotiable; code beyond it is no longer a virtue.

### Changed
- **`scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-completeness-section.ts`**: the default section reads "Complete coverage, minimal code": recommend full coverage of the requirement (tests, edge cases, error paths) and no code beyond it, prefer the smaller diff at equal coverage, and add no checks for impossible states. Unrelated work stays separate scope. The `Completeness: X/10` scoring rule and the GPT-5.6 Sol variant are unchanged. The section is 3 characters shorter, so every regenerated skill shrinks and 89 size pins go down.
- **`ETHOS.md`**: "Completeness is cheap ... always prefer A" becomes "Complete coverage, minimal code": completeness is measured in coverage, not lines; at equal coverage choose the smaller diff; no speculative abstractions, impossible-state checks or unneeded refactors. A new anti-pattern names the impossible-state fallback. Section 1's opener now says "When covering the whole requirement costs minutes more than the shortcut, cover it. Every time. Complete means complete coverage, not more code.", and "How They Work Together" says Boil the Ocean means "cover the whole requirement with the least code" instead of "do the complete thing".
- **`plan-ceo-review/SKILL.md.tmpl`**: the Philosophy bullet "COMPLETENESS IS CHEAP: AI makes 70 LOC seconds. Prefer complete ~150 LOC over 90% ~80 LOC. Boil the ocean." becomes "COMPLETENESS IS COVERAGE": cover the whole requirement (tests, edge cases, error paths) rather than a 90% shortcut, add no code beyond the accepted scope (so SCOPE EXPANSION and SELECTIVE EXPANSION still build what the user accepted), and choose the smaller diff at equal coverage. plan-ceo-review is under the 100,000-character limit on every host and has no size pin, so it grows about 100 characters without a pin change.
- **First-run intro**: the one-time Boil the Ocean intro in `bin/gstack-skill-start` says "complete coverage, minimal code" instead of "do the complete thing when AI makes marginal cost near-zero". The agents digest's Boil the Ocean bullet (`scripts/gen-agents-digest.ts`, regenerated `agents-digest/gstack-AGENTS.md`) says the same: "complete coverage, minimal code: cover the whole requirement (tests, edge cases, error paths) and write no code beyond it".
- `review/specialists/simplification.md` quotes the new house rule instead of "If A is 70 lines more, choose A", and `CLAUDE.md` restates it in place of "Completeness is cheap ... the complete thing is the goal".

### Tests
- `test/model-overlays.test.ts` asserts the new default wording ("Complete coverage, minimal code.", "prefer the smaller diff") and checks, one sentence per rule, that the section still states full coverage of the requirement with no code beyond it, the smaller diff only at equal coverage, no checks for impossible states, and that unrelated work is separate scope that never excuses a gap.
- `test/ceo-workflow-clarity.test.ts` checks that the plan-ceo-review Philosophy bullet still asks for the whole requirement over a 90% shortcut, no code beyond the accepted scope and the smaller diff at equal coverage, and that "COMPLETENESS IS CHEAP" and "~150 LOC" stay gone.
- `test/gen-skill-docs.test.ts` checks that the house rule `review/specialists/simplification.md` quotes is still stated in ETHOS.md. `test/gstack-skill-start.test.ts` checks that the first-run intro says complete coverage, minimal code and never "do the complete thing".
- `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json`: 89 pins lowered by 3 characters each. None raised; the plan-ceo-review rewording touches no pinned skill.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, budget, timeout, trial count, case kind or assertion weakened. The section heading "Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean" is unchanged.

## [1.91.274.0] - 2026-10-27

**/design-html and /design-review now run the design lint, and its copy tier reports every content and ship-floor tell at its line (hallmark phase 2, GSTA-92; Garry 2026-10-26 "Do it", option a).** The two design skills still called `gstack-design-craft`, which counted tells without positions and kept accepted exceptions in finalized.json. The lint already carried the same ids, so the skills now call it, the copy tier has its own patterns with line numbers, and a page answers a tell with a waiver comment beside it instead of a side record.

### Changed
- **/design-html** Step 4 runs `gstack-design-lint <page> --render` after the Slop Gate and reads its exit code: 2 fixes every `blocks` line, 1 fixes or waives each `ask` line, 0 lists `polish` as notes. A missing `LINT_SUMMARY`, a `render` line or `render=skipped` is said plainly and the static lines stand.
- **Waivers live in the page.** A real customer named Nexus or a supplied 50% figure gets `<!-- gstack-lint-disable <rule-id>: <reason about this page, 24+ chars> -->`, written only for what the user supplied or confirmed. This supersedes #3422's persisted craft exceptions: `--accepted` and finalized.json's `craft_exceptions` are gone, and the hand-off lists every waiver.
- **Copy-tier tiers**: `placeholder-name`, `placeholder-brand`, `lorem`, `round-number` and `needs-proof` move from blocks to ask, so the waiver above can answer them. /design-review still files a waived `needs-proof` or `lorem`, which a live page cannot carry.
- **/design-review's craft audit** runs the lint on each saved page: `blocks` and `ask` lines are category 9 findings at their line, `waived` lines are listed with their reason, `empty-mount-node` sends the audit to the saved DOM. A saved live page has lost its linked CSS, so the audit files only its copy-tier (`craft`) lines there and judges the CSS rules by eye.
- **`lib/design-lint/rules/copy.ts`** holds the copy tier's own patterns (moved from `lib/design-craft.ts`), reporting each tell at its line with what matched. It reads visible text, script bodies and inline handlers (single-quoted included) and the parsed tags, so a hydration payload, commented-out markup or a `<title>` string inside a script no longer counts.

### Added
- **`empty-mount-node`** (ask, page only): a body with no text, a `<noscript>` notice aside, that loads a script is a client-rendered shell; the lint says it read none of its content instead of passing it.

## [1.91.273.0] - 2026-10-27

**A PR body opens with the problem it solves, says what else it touches, and the prose /ship publishes is checked for autopilot tells before it goes out.** A /ship PR body began with a list of what changed, so a reader had to work out the problem from the inventory; nothing in the body said what else the change could break or how sure the author was that it would not; and a CHANGELOG entry or PR body could carry the words a model writes when it is not thinking (`a vibrant tapestry of enhancements`, `not just X, but Y`, an arrow where a sentence belongs) because nothing checked prose mechanically. Garry approved the tstack and pstack absorb plans on 2026-10-26 ("Do it, send"); this release carries tstack item 4 and pstack items 2(a) and 11.

### Added
- **`bin/gstack-prose-lint`, `lib/prose-lint.ts`**: the AI tells a regular expression can decide, as a free check over the files it is given. Eight rules: `vocabulary` (the autopilot word list), `not-just-but`, `metaphor-noun` (each with the plain word to use), `mid-sentence-colon` (a colon doing a conjunction's job; a label, a list introducer or a time is not one), `inline-header-list` (a bold label that restates its line), `arrow` (a measurement such as `1.6740 → 1.7010` and the `before → after` heading pass), `dropped-article` (a bare noun opening a sentence, with compound nouns such as test runs and merge commits left alone) and `unclosed-block` (a fence or HTML comment left open, since nothing after it was read). Fenced code, inline code, URLs, HTML comments and quoted words are never read, so the problem a `## Why` quotes stays in the person's words. `--unreleased` reads only a CHANGELOG's `## [Unreleased]` block, `--base <ref>` only the lines the working tree added since the merge base, and `--sections <a,b>` only the text under those `## ` headings, so an older entry or a verbatim tool section is never judged; `--gate` turns a finding into exit 1 with `PROSE_LINT_FOUND` ([docs/troubleshooting.md#prose-lint-found](docs/troubleshooting.md#prose-lint-found)); without it the run is a report and exits 0. gstack's own templates and docs keep their em dashes, because the lint gates only the CHANGELOG entry and the PR body sections the author writes. The word lists come from pstack's unslop skill (Lauren Tan, MIT; NOTICE.md), the rules are written in gstack's words.
- **`## Blast radius` in the /ship PR body** (`ship/sections/pr-body.md`, and `capy-pr.md` after `## Why` on the Capy path): one or two sentences on what else the change touches and the one fact that makes that safe, with the rung of the evidence ladder the fact reached (a file:line read, a walked failure path, a script that ran, a repro). The ladder itself is the `/investigate` skill's Blast radius section once its own lane lands; until then the item's inline rung list is the ladder.
- **Quality gate workflow step**: `gstack-prose-lint CHANGELOG.md --unreleased --gate` runs on every PR over the `[Unreleased]` block, which is the entry the PR adds until the train stamps it; a stamped or absent block is `none` and passes.

### Changed
- **`ship/sections/pr-body.md` Step 19 `## Summary`**: the first paragraph states the problem in the user's words, then the fix and what they get now; commit themes follow, and the body is never an inventory or a commit list. The instruction carries one BAD/GOOD pair. Step 18's new-PR title keeps its `v<version>` prefix and the text after it names what the user gets, not the mechanism. The compose block runs `gstack-prose-lint --sections 'Why,Summary,Blast radius' --gate` over the first body draft before the drafts are joined, so a review line such as `Problem → what you did`, an approvals row or an image's text is never read, a finding in a section the author wrote stops composition with the lines to rewrite, and a draft that lost one of those headings is a usage error rather than a pass.
- **`ship/sections/capy-pr.md` `## Why`**: the first sentence quotes the person's problem, the rest say what changes for them, with its own BAD/GOOD pair; the section order gains `## Blast radius`.
- **`ship/sections/changelog.md` Step 13**: item 7 lints the lines this branch added to `CHANGELOG.md` (`--base origin/<base> --gate`) and the entry is rewritten until the trailer is `PROSE_LINT: ok`.

### Tests
- `test/prose-lint.test.ts`: one positive and one negative case per rule, masking of code, URLs and comments with line numbers held, the `--unreleased` and `--base` selections against a fixture CHANGELOG and a temporary repository, the exit codes and the `PROSE_LINT_FOUND` line, the `--sections` selection, a multi-line HTML comment masked through its close, the template and workflow wiring, and the templates themselves getting a report rather than a gate. Fixtures: `test/fixtures/prose-lint/{slopped,clean}-changelog.md`.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, timeout, trial count or case kind changed. The ship parity `maxSizeRatio` in `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts` moves 1.7400 → 1.7500 (measured 328,319 / 187,706 = 1.7491 on the tree with v1.91.270.0 merged) for the pr-body, capy-pr and changelog section text above; this lane leaves the ship skeleton untouched, so no host pin in `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json` moves. The raise is this lane's own call, made under Garry's 2026-10-26 "Do it, send" on the two absorb plans (which budget these ship sections; the quote approves the plans, not the number); the skeleton is unchanged, so no host pin moves.

## [1.91.271.0] - 2026-10-27

**The merge-train bisect can run in CI.** Every `train-bisect` job of `evals.yml` had died at its first step: a container job's `run` steps default to `sh -e {0}` (dash in the CI image), and "Verify the prefix checkout" used the bash-only `${PREFIX_SHA:0:12}`, so run 40456150409 (the first bisect ever dispatched, gate.bisect-b3d085bb87ee-d9b0d60082cc) failed all three prefixes with `Bad substitution` (exit 2) before a case ran; the second bisect run was cancelled. The job shipped in 1.91.162.0 (GSTA-49 T1b) and had never passed. Found while GSTA-96's auq-format-gate red put a train on the bisect path.

### Fixed
- **`.github/workflows/evals.yml` `train-bisect`**: the job declares `defaults.run.shell: bash`, so every one of its run steps runs under `bash -e -o pipefail` like the steps on bare runners do. No other run step whose effective shell is sh uses a bash construct (the new lint below checked all 23 of them across `evals.yml`, `evals-periodic.yml`, `evals-marathon.yml` and `eval-sweep.yml`).

### Tests
- `test/workflow-shell-lint.test.ts` (new, free, offline): parses every workflow under `.github/workflows/` and every composite action under `.github/actions/`, computes each run step's effective shell (step `shell` → job `defaults.run.shell` → workflow `defaults.run.shell` → GitHub's default: sh in a container job, pwsh on Windows, bash otherwise), and fails on a bash-only construct in a step whose effective shell is sh (`${x:0:n}`, `${x//…}`, `${!x}`, `[[`, arrays, `declare -a`/`mapfile`, `set -o pipefail`, `PIPESTATUS`, `<<<`, `<(…)`, `$'…'`, `source`, `function`). The detector has positive controls for each construct and negative controls for the POSIX forms (`${x:-d}`, `${x#p}`, `$(…)`, `$((…))`, comments). A fourth test pins the `train-bisect` job to bash by name; it was red at d9b0d60 and is green with the fix.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, trial count, case kind, budget or reservation changed; the bisect's cases, prefixes and spend path are untouched. The job's run steps gain `pipefail` from bash's explicit-shell default; the one that pipes (the Codex login) already ran under `shell: bash` with `set -euo pipefail`, and the others run single commands.

## [1.91.270.0] - 2026-10-27

### Added
- **Repositories without a version source** (`ship/SKILL.md` Step 12, `ship/sections/changelog.md`, `gstack-ship-receipt write`): a repo with no `.gstack/version-path` pin and no `VERSION` ships without a version change: `Version bump: skipped (no version source: <path, reason>)`, no `VERSION` is ever created, the PR title is unprefixed and the run log records `"version":null`; the receipt records `"version": "none"` when the repo also has no `package.json#version`, no policy stamp file and no CHANGELOG. A repo with no CHANGELOG (the policy's `changelog` is null or the file is absent) prints `CHANGELOG: skipped (none at <path>)` and never creates the file ([ship-policy.md#ship-receipt](docs/ship-policy.md#ship-receipt)).
- **Docs audit record and doc caps** (`lib/ship-receipt-docs.ts`, `gstack-ship-receipt write --docs <json|@file>`, `gstack-ship-receipt docs-caps [--base <ref>] [--policy <file>]`, policy key `docs.caps: [{ path, max_bytes }]`): Step 14.5's outcome (`updated` | `current` | `blocked`, with the owner's `exception: { accepted_by, date, via, reason }`) is part of the receipt; `blocked` without an exception, or a `--body` that lacks the exception line word for word, refuses with `DOCS_AUDIT_BLOCKED`; a declared doc over its byte cap (or absent) prints `DOCS_CAP: <path> <bytes>/<max> over` and blocks before the verification gate; the caps come from `origin/<base>`'s policy, never the branch's copy, so a PR cannot raise its own cap, and an unreadable base policy refuses with `POLICY_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` (`--policy <file>` is for a repository bootstrapping its policy). The `docs` key needs `min_gstack_version` (`DOCS_CAPS_KEY_VERSION`, the release that stamps this entry).

- **`gstack-ship-receipt write`** records `version: "none"` only when the repository has no version source at all; a `VERSION` that exists but holds no parsable version, a pin that escapes the repository or an unreadable base policy keeps the no-version refusal. `checkReceiptProse` matches a shared leaf key (`pass` under every gate lane) against any of its counters and never inside a longer word (`3 pass-through`).

## [1.91.268.0] - 2026-10-27

**Two read-and-write helpers absorbed from pstack: a decision trail a reviewer reads without the transcript, and a worktree audit that tells you which Conductor worktrees are safe to remove.** Both are ports of Lauren Tan's MIT scripts (header credit in each file, `licenses/MIT-pstack.txt`, NOTICE.md), approved with the rest of the pstack absorb (Garry, 2026-10-26: "Do it, send").

### Added
- **`bin/gstack-decision-trail <file> <phase> <decision> <why> <evidence> <result>`**: appends one UTC-stamped row to a run's TSV decision trail, writing the header once and only ever appending; cells are flattened to one line and a cell that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` gets a leading quote so evidence lifted from a PR title or a filename cannot run as a formula in a reviewer's spreadsheet. `start <file> <run-id>` appends a run's `start` row (naming the earlier rows and `run:<id>`; the id is letters, digits and `. _ : @ / -`, so a tab or quote in it is a usage error rather than a row that breaks the idempotence check) and is a no-op while that row is the newest start row, so a rerun writes nothing twice; only a leading `-h`/`--help` is help, so a cell whose text is `-h` is appended as data; a trail without a final newline, with CRLF rows, a UTF-8 BOM, a repeated header line or no header at all is appended to correctly; `--run <id>` on an append refuses with `DECISION_TRAIL_START_REQUIRED` (exit 3) until the run has opened its stretch. The end-of-run rule, in `docs/unattended.md` ("The decision trail") and `autoplan/DRIVER.md`: audit the trail against the transcript and correct the log, not the story (a wrong row is superseded, never edited), then a reviewer on another model family reads it and the report ends with an `Attention` section (`reviewed by <model>`, the flags, or `No flags`).
- **`bin/gstack-worktree-audit [-b <ref>] [--no-fetch] [repo]`** (bash, read-only): one TSV row per git worktree beside the main one, largest first: size, age, merged into the base, `clean`/`wip:<n>`/`scratch:<n>`, `pushed`/`ahead<n>`/`no-remote`/`detached`, the PR on its branch through `gh`'s own `--jq` (no `jq` needed), the newest Claude Code chat that ran in the worktree (`${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/projects/<slug>`) and a bucket: `prunable` (registered, directory gone), `hold-wip`, `hold-open-pr`, `verify-recent-chat`, `safe`, `review`. `safe` means nothing exists only in that worktree: a clean tree that is merged into the base or whose PR is closed or merged with every commit pushed; an unpushed commit or an untracked file on a merged branch reads `review`. A fork's PR on a same-named branch is ignored and an open PR wins over an older closed one on a reused name. A locked entry whose directory is gone and a `broken` worktree whose own `.git` link is missing (git would otherwise describe the containing repository and hide its files) read `review`; a clean tree names its gitignored entries as `clean,ignored:<n>` without changing the bucket; a branch name shared with a tag still resolves; worktree paths with leading, trailing or inner spaces are read whole. It never deletes or prunes; its one write is a best-effort fetch of the base ref that `--no-fetch` skips. `/landing-report` offers it when the sibling table shows stale worktrees; `docs/CONTRIBUTOR_REFERENCE.md` has the guide for Conductor users, `docs/standalone-binaries.md` lists both bins.

### Tests
- `test/decision-trail.test.ts`: header once (an empty file gets one, a second append does not), the formula guard on every leading byte it covers, flattened tabs and line breaks, the start row's text and its idempotent rerun, a second run's start row, the `--run` refusal and admission, a `-h` cell appended as data, a missing final newline, CRLF rows and a repeated header, a blank file and a BOM, run ids with whitespace or quotes refused, usage errors.
- `test/worktree-audit.test.ts`: a bare origin, a clone and twelve worktrees (merged, wip with an open PR, scratch with a chat today, stale, closed PR, a merged one whose path has a space, a merged one with only an untracked file, a registered one whose directory is gone, a locked one whose directory is gone, a broken one inside the clone with a precious file, one whose branch shares its name with a tag, one with only a gitignored `.env`) classified into every bucket (also under `status.showUntrackedFiles=no`, which must not hide untracked files) through a fake `gh` (which records its arguments and runs the audit's own `--jq` over canned JSON with a fork PR when `jq` is installed) and a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` transcript directory; the fixture, its worktree registry included, is byte-identical after the audit; `-b`, `--no-fetch`, an unpushed commit on a closed PR reading `review` and an open PR on the reused name winning, no `gh` on PATH (git resolved from `git --exec-path`, so a distribution's wrapper script does not matter), a failing `gh`, a missing base and a non-repo path.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, timeout, trial count or case kind changed. No pinned skill changed; `landing-report/SKILL.md` grows by one line and is unpinned. `test/autoplan-driver.test.ts`'s line cap on `autoplan/DRIVER.md` moves 160 → 162 (measured 162) for the decision-trail paragraph at the end of the coordinator contract section; the file was at the cap before.

## [1.91.266.0] - 2026-10-27

### Added
- **`bin/gstack-pr-wait`, `lib/pr-wait.ts`, `lib/pr-wait-github.ts`**: an event-driven pull-request watcher (design ported from tstack's pr-wait, MIT, Theo Browne; NOTICE.md, `licenses/MIT-tstack.txt`). `gstack-pr-wait <pr> [--repo owner/name] [--until green|ready|any-change] [--interval SECONDS] [--timeout MINUTES]` prints one stdout line per real event, prefixed `#<pr>`, and progress on stderr: a check failed (name and link), all checks finished on the head, a comment, review, thread or reply from someone other than the PR author or the gh user, a review bot finished on the head or a gating bot's summary changed, the base branch moved and its new commits touch this PR's files, merge state BEHIND or DIRTY, merged or closed. `green` gates on every check on the head, as `gstack-ci-gate` does, so Step 2 and Step 3 of `/land-and-deploy` never disagree; a check the base branch requires (rulesets and classic branch protection) is pending until it appears, never green by omission, and two identical polls confirm the check set. `ready` is green plus a gating bot's review of the head (green alone when no gating bot is configured), no unresolved thread, and a known merge state (GitHub's `UNKNOWN` right after a push holds it); a gating bot's failed check is a failed check, never a review. A bot owns the logins that start with its name (`greptile-apps[bot]`, not `notgreptile`) and the checks that mention it. `--timeout` (default 60 minutes, 0 for none) ends a watch that met nothing as blocked, naming the still-pending checks; at `/land-and-deploy` Step 3 that is a STOP showing the line, and the user decides whether to start again with a larger `--timeout` or `--timeout 0`. Exit 0 when the condition is met or the PR merged, 1 when it needs action (`PR_WAIT_BLOCKED`), 2 on bad input, an unreadable PR, a second watcher for the same PR or a local error (`PR_WAIT_REFUSED`; a lock whose pid is dead is taken over), so exit 1 always carries a `PR_WAIT_BLOCKED` line. The loop is synchronous and installs no signal handlers, so Ctrl-C and `kill` stop it at once. State lives under `<state root>/pr-wait/` (lib/state-root.ts chain), and a baseline older than 6 hours is discarded. Transient gh failures (5xx, 429, network, gh's own 60 s spawn timeout) retry with backoff; ten failed polls in a row end the watch as blocked. BEHIND and DIRTY are announced once per head (keyed on the head alone, so a base that keeps moving does not repeat them), with the short head in the line. A verdict whose state file cannot be written keeps its exit code; the save error goes to stderr.
- **`gstack-config` keys `pr_wait_gating_bots` (default `greptile,macroscope`) and `pr_wait_advisory_bots` (default `coderabbit`)**: which review bots `--until ready` waits for and which it only reports; comma-separated names matched against bot logins and check names, `none` empties a list, anything else is rejected with the value kept.
- **Result codes `PR_WAIT_BLOCKED` and `PR_WAIT_REFUSED`** (`lib/result-codes-release.ts`) with their [troubleshooting anchors](docs/troubleshooting.md#gstack-pr-wait); a `gstack-pr-wait` row in docs/standalone-binaries.md.

### Changed
- **`/land-and-deploy` Step 3**: the 4-minute `gstack-ci-gate --wait 240` polling rounds with a 15-minute cap and a wait-more/exclude/stop question are replaced by one `gstack-pr-wait "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$REPO" --until green` call; exit 0 reruns Step 2's gate on the pinned head, exit 1 stops with the watcher's lines (a red `required=n` check stays the one case Step 3.5 may approve), exit 2 shows the refusal. The Important Rules line about polling intervals names the watcher. The old 15-minute cap becomes the watcher's `--timeout` default of 60 minutes; the wait-more question is gone, a timeout stops Step 3 with the pending checks named. The generated skill is the same size on every pinned host, so no pin moved.

### Tests

## [1.91.265.0] - 2026-10-27

**Four more principles, and three places gstack stops asking what it could observe (pstack absorb, lane C3, GSTA-124).** Ideas from Lauren Tan's pstack (MIT), written in gstack's words; NOTICE.md and the ETHOS.md credit line say so.

### Added
- **ETHOS.md principles 5 to 8**: Attack the Premise (two fixes that share a premise and fail the same gate indict the premise; write it down and falsify it before a third fix), Separate Before Serializing Shared State (a lock is a smell to check; remove the race before refereeing it), Make Operations Idempotent (design for the run that happens twice; ask what happens if the previous run died at every point), Explain the Number (a measurement carries what was measured, the limiter it moved and the run-to-run variation; a gap inside the variation is no difference). "How They Work Together" gains one line each and a Credits section names the source.
- **`/eval-plan` Step 1c, candidate-side blinding**: three preregistration rules (no eval word anywhere the candidate can read; project-shaped fixture roots; the judge sees `A`/`B` labels and grades chain-following from the files the transcript shows the candidate opened). `prereg --check` does not read fixture trees, and the step says so. `docs/TESTING_INTERNALS.md#candidate-side-blinding` states the same rules for gstack's own fixtures, lists the fixture directory names on the word list and the candidate-visible temporary roots it found (`arm-<fixture>-<arm>-*` from `test/helpers/arm-benchmark-harness.ts`, `skill-e2e-benchmark-*` from `test/skill-e2e-deploy.test.ts`, the `skill-e2e-<id>-*` roots of `test/skill-e2e-test-value.test.ts` whose ids carry `test`, `gstack-health-eval-*` from `test/skill-e2e-health.test.ts`; the list is a scan of `mkdtemp` prefixes in e2e tests, not a proof of completeness); no fixture is renamed here.
- **Observable questions are not the user's to answer**: a rule in `/plan-tune`'s Important Rules and a section in `docs/proactive.md`. A question a local, read-only, free command, render or measurement can settle is settled that way and reported (a call that changes state, reaches a live or third-party system or spends money stays a question); only product and preference calls reach the user, with the observation already made. The question-log audit treats an observable question as a defect in the asking skill rather than a preference to tune.

### Changed
- **AGENTS.md validation discipline step 4**: one sentence on measured deltas: name the limiter that moved and the run-to-run variation; a gap smaller than that variation is no difference. `agents-digest/gstack-AGENTS.md` is generated from `scripts/gen-agents-digest.ts` and `VERSION`, not from AGENTS.md, so the regenerated digest is unchanged.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, trial count, case kind or judge prompt changed. Prose-only change: `plan-tune` and `eval-plan` are unpinned skills; sizes measured in the PR body.

## [1.91.264.0] - 2026-10-27

**/design-motion turns an approved design into a showcase loop for X and the website; adapted from Elaya's design-to-motion (GSTA-92 plan item 15, Garry 2026-10-25 "Do it").** gstack could design a screen and build it, but not show it moving: a screen recording drops frames, jumps at the loop seam, and nothing tells you a card drifted out of its container. /design-motion rebuilds the exact frame from a /design-shotgun PNG, a /design-html `finalized.html` or a URL (a Figma link when `FIGMA_TOKEN` is set), loads it from an empty state, gives each visual one story, records frames on a fake clock, and exports only after the loop is proven seamless.

### Added
- **/design-motion** (new skill; sections `fidelity`, `motion`, and `figma` read only with a Figma token, which reaches curl on stdin so it never appears in a process list). Showcase context: every visual gets a story, the cycle ends in a dissolve and an empty beat. Website context: gstack's rules win, so one authored motion moment per page, content complete without script and under reduced motion, an `IntersectionObserver` start, and no pulse, marquee or caret left running.
- **`bin/gstack-motion-capture.ts`** (`lib/motion-capture.ts`): Playwright with its fake clock and gstack's own Chromium (`GSTACK_CHROMIUM_PATH` honoured). Steps are whole milliseconds averaging 1000/60, so the seam frame is exactly one cycle after the window start. The page contract is `window.__start()`, `window.__tick(dt)` and `window.__lt`, with 15 PRE frames before the start. Writes `frames/`, `still.png`, an optional container `mask.png` and `capture.json`.
- **`bin/gstack-motion-encode`** (`lib/motion-encode.ts`): `check` prints `MOTION_CHECK:` lines for seam, empty beat, rest and overflow (ffmpeg PSNR, identical means `inf`), writes a contact sheet, and ends `MOTION_RESULT: clean` or `<n> failed`. `export` writes `<name>-x.mp4` (H.264, CRF 15, 60 fps), `<name>-loop.gif` (960 px, 20 fps) and `<name>-800x500.gif` with Elaya's recipes. `compare` gives the still-fidelity PSNR. ffmpeg is optional: without it the bin prints `FFMPEG_MISSING` with install commands and exits 3.
- Both bins refuse bad input before any work: `gstack-motion-encode` exits 2 on an unknown option or `--formats` token, a `--pad` that is not a 6- or 8-digit hex colour, a `--crop` that is not `w:h:x:y` (`compare` included, so nothing but a colour or a crop reaches ffmpeg's filter graph) and a capture whose frames are missing. `check` prints a `MOTION_SETTINGS:` line naming any threshold or phase override, so a relaxed run never looks like a strict one, a capture without a mask ends `MOTION_RESULT: clean (overflow not checked)`, and the contact sheet no longer needs ffmpeg 5.1's `-fps_mode`. `gstack-motion-capture.ts` refuses a `--cycle` that is not a multiple of 0.05 s (three 60 fps frames; only then does the seam land exactly one cycle later for every PRE) and an `--out` that holds a still or frames but not its `.gstack-motion-capture` marker, so a rerun after a failed capture works and a foreign directory is never cleared. `check` and `export` refuse a `capture.json` whose fields are not what the capture writes (they reach ffmpeg arguments and paths), and a cards overflow check with no story frames is an error instead of a pass. When an app frame's own surfaces cover more than 90% of the frame (full bleed), overflow is reported as skipped and the run ends `clean (overflow not checked)`; the same coverage in a cards layout, or reached only through `--mask-grow`, fails overflow instead of passing by blacking out everything; a `--mask` that matches no element stops the capture with `MOTION_MASK_EMPTY`; `--mask-grow` is a whole number from 0 to 32, and `--mask` refuses anything but a selector. Offscreen `loading="lazy"` images no longer hang a render, font or image loading is bounded at 30 s, and a frame whose `__tick` never returns fails after 10 s with `MOTION_CAPTURE_FAILED`. A CSS transition a story starts with a class toggle is seeked from the frame it appears rather than from the last `__mark`, so it eases in the export instead of popping. An empty numeric option (`--min-db ''`) is refused instead of read as 0, and the Figma section only fills a file key and node id that look like Figma's. Exports write to a `.partial-` file and rename on success, so a failed re-export never truncates the last good file; a `--gif-fps` or `--small-fps` above 50 or not dividing the cycle is refused instead of drifting; `compare` resolves its paths; a `GSTACK_FFMPEG` that names a missing file says so. A URL source is treated as untrusted data. A capture now clears the previous run's manifest and stills along with its frames, scales a portrait frame to 1200×1920, renders stills with CSS animations finished, and tolerates a page that takes longer than 10 s to load.

### Tests
- `test/motion-capture.test.ts`, `test/motion-encode.test.ts`: step and clock math (the seam frame lands exactly one cycle later for every PRE and cycle tried), argument errors, the exact export recipes, check frame selection for both layouts, PSNR parsing and verdicts (fewer compared frames than planned fails), and the `FFMPEG_MISSING` path, all without a browser, ffmpeg or network.
- `test/motion-pipeline.test.ts`: a 0.5 s fixture loop goes through capture, check, export and compare on real Chromium and ffmpeg, a page that does not loop and a page without the capture contract fail with their named reasons, and the same non-looping capture checks clean under `--min-db 0` only with that override printed. The same `--out` is refused while it holds foreign files, accepts the retry after a refused page, and reports `clean (overflow not checked)` without a mask; a page with an offscreen lazy image renders its still at `--scale 2`; a full-frame mask fails a cards check and is not checked for an app frame, and an empty mask stops the capture before any frame; a spinning `__tick` fails after 10 s; a class-toggled story transition is mid-fade at its midpoint frame; a blank `--min-db` is refused; a failed re-export keeps the last good GIF and a drifting `--gif-fps` is refused. It skips itself when Chromium, ffmpeg or ffprobe is missing. The motion unit tests add the new refusals and a portrait scale.
- New paid case `design-motion-showcase` (`test/skill-e2e-design.test.ts`): a finalized page goes through rebuild, capture, checks and export, and the agent must read the fidelity and motion sections and run `check` before `export`. The design-motion carve guard points at it. It runs in the marathon tier as a 3-trial behavior panel, because the periodic census is at its 38-slice cap and three 3-6 minute trials would add two slices; it needs ffmpeg and Chromium on the runner. Its section-read and ordering checks accept a full `cat` of a section and capture, check and export in one Bash call (a free replay of the first panel's three captures passes; a `grep` of a section, no `check`, and export before check still fail).

## [1.91.263.0] - 2026-10-27

**Merge trains read their screens from the run, follow themselves without a daemon, and refuse what would have cost a gate.** Operating trains on 2026-10-26 showed the gaps: two screens were VERDICT RED while their lanes reported green and the heads were READY'd anyway; 18 of 41 PR screens concluded success with no slice; a PR whose merge ref lagged main could not be screened at all (#3465); two trains whose PRs merged elsewhere sat in `merging`/`green` forever; a background `gh run watch` chain died with every machine restart; a PR's new tests passed on its branch and failed once stacked behind another PR; and the four-step hand procedure for a conflicting PR's CI was typed by hand each time.

### Added
- **`lib/ship-queue-screen.ts`**: a dispatched screen's verdict is read from the run's own artifacts (`gate-binding-a<attempt>`: verdict, reconcile exit, flaky cases; `report-verdict-a<attempt>/paid-report/collector-outcomes.json`: the panels that failed the lane and the rule-16 flaky lines; a confirmed verdict reuse in `paid-plan/gate-reuse.json`), never from a lane's prose. `ready --screen`, `verify --pr <n> --screen` and `train build` print `SCREEN_VERDICT: #<n> run <id> GREEN|RED|NOT-RUN|INCOMPLETE [red=…] [flaky=…]` plus one `FLAKY:` line per flaky case, and record the verdict in the READY receipt (`screen.verdict`, locally and in `refs/notes/gstack-trains`).
- **`QUEUE_SCREEN_RED`**: a RED screen refuses `ready` under `--screen` and `--no-screen` alike, is never re-dispatched at the same merge SHA, and `train build` refuses to seat the pin. **`QUEUE_SCREEN_NOT_RUN`**: a screen run that concluded success with no slice (its route job found the head superseded by a push, or the plan selected nothing) is `NOT-RUN`: `verify --screen` refuses, the receipt records `NOT_RUN`, `ready --screen` dispatches afresh instead of following it, and `train build` seats the pin unscreened with a `SCREEN: … counted as not-run` line.
- **Scratch-merge screens (#3465)**: when GitHub's `refs/pull/<n>/merge` lags the PR head, is missing or cannot be fetched, `ready --screen` plans the screen on a scratch merge of the head onto the base, pushed as `screen/<pr>-<head12>` (`SCREEN_MERGE:` names it); only a real conflict with the base (or a remote whose refs cannot be listed) is `QUEUE_SCREEN_STALE_REF`, whose text now says so, and a base that cannot be fetched is `POLICY_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`.
- **`train watch --train <nonce> [--timeout <s>]`** (`lib/ship-queue-train-watch.ts`): the one resumable follow command. It reads the record, runs the step its state asks for (`train build --train` to push, run the free tests and dispatch the gate; `train status` to settle an unconfirmed dispatch), waits for the pending run by polling gh, reads the verdict and prints the last step's `NEXT:`. No process state: rerun it after an interruption and it continues from the record; it never dispatches anything the record would not dispatch on its own.
- **`train prune --stale`**: a `merging` or `green` train whose every PR is MERGED or CLOSED on GitHub is marked `stale` (a new terminal state), its branch deleted, each PR's state logged on a `STALE:` line; a train with an OPEN PR is kept and says why. The same run deletes every `screen/<pr>-*` scratch branch whose PR is MERGED or CLOSED. **`train forget --train <nonce> | --receipt <pr>@<sha> [--dry-run]`** (`lib/ship-queue-train-forget.ts`) removes one settled train (attempts included) or one READY receipt from local state and from the notes ref with an exact `--force-with-lease` on `refs/notes/gstack-trains`; a train still building, running or merging is refused, and a rejected lease removes nothing.
- **`verify --post-merge <sha> [--timeout <s>]`** (`lib/ship-queue-post-merge.ts`): after a merge, waits for every check run and commit status attached to the merged commit (its full 40-hex SHA) to settle, prints one `CHECK: <name> <conclusion>` per check and `POST_MERGE: <sha12> green|red|pending|none (passed= failed= pending= skipped=)`; green needs a completed check and no failure, `neutral`/`skipped` count as skipped, a pending commit status keeps it pending, a failed check or status is **`QUEUE_POST_MERGE_RED`**, a timeout is `QUEUE_TRAIN_PENDING` with the same command as `NEXT:`.
- **`ready … --dispatch-ci <wf.yml[,…]> [--timeout <s>]`** (`lib/ship-queue-dispatch-ci.ts`): for a PR that conflicts with the base and so has no pull_request CI, dispatches each named workflow on the branch (skipped when a run at this head already concluded), waits for the runs (`CI_DISPATCH:` lines), clears every requires-remote pregate lane whose workflow is one of them with the run URL (`PREGATE_CLEARED:`), then reads the head as usual. A red run clears no lane and refuses; a fork head is `QUEUE_TRAIN_UNTRUSTED`. This replaces the four-step hand procedure in docs/ship-policy.md.
- **`train build --dry-run --stack-tests [--stack-tests-command "<cmd>"]`** (`lib/ship-queue-stack-tests.ts`): runs each PR's new test files on the integrated prefix that includes it (T<k>) in a scratch worktree and prints `STACK_TESTS: #<pr> T<k> <n> new test file(s) pass|FAIL (<files>)` or `no new test files`; a failure is **`QUEUE_TRAIN_STACK_RED`** with nothing written, pushed or dispatched.

### Changed
- **`lib/ship-queue-train-github.ts`**: `downloadJson` finds a named file anywhere in a multi-path artifact (`report-verdict-a1` keeps its `paid-report/` directory). **`lib/ship-queue.ts`**: `ciAtHead` is exported and returns the per-check list it already read. **`scripts/lib/windows-curation.ts`**: `test/ship-queue-train-ops.test.ts` is excluded from the Windows subset like the other gh-shim drivers.
- docs/ship-policy.md's merge-train section documents every command above; docs/troubleshooting.md gains `QUEUE_SCREEN_RED`, `QUEUE_SCREEN_NOT_RUN`, `QUEUE_TRAIN_STACK_RED` and `QUEUE_POST_MERGE_RED`, and `QUEUE_SCREEN_STALE_REF` now means a real conflict only.

### Tests
- `test/ship-queue-train-ops.test.ts` (new; the gh shim in `test/helpers/ship-queue-train-fixture.ts` gained `binding`, `outcomes`, `reuse`, `plan: null` and `ci` rules with the real artifact layout): a RED screen refuses ready under either choice, is printed by verify --screen with its red and flaky cases and refuses the pin in train build; a GREEN screen with flaky cases is followed and recorded; a NOT-RUN screen refuses verify with `QUEUE_SCREEN_NOT_RUN`, records `NOT_RUN` and is re-dispatched; a lagging or missing merge ref gets a scratch merge as `screen/<pr>-<head12>` and a real conflict stays `QUEUE_SCREEN_STALE_REF`; prune --stale settles only an all-merged-or-closed train and keeps one with an OPEN PR; train forget removes a train or a receipt and refuses a merging train; watch resumes from free-pending through the gate to the verdict and never dispatches twice; verify --post-merge waits, is red with the failed names, green when settled, resumable after a timeout; ready --dispatch-ci dispatches, waits, clears the matching lanes, refuses a red run and a fork head; --stack-tests catches a PR whose new test fails on T2 and passes after `--order` moves it first. Each was red before its change.
- `test/ship-queue-train.test.ts`: the stale-ref test now proves the scratch merge path; the planned-0-cases test expects the SCREEN: verdict lines.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, rubric, trial count, case kind or judge prompt changed. A screen's verdict is read as evals.yml bound it; nothing here changes what a case must pass.

## [1.91.262.0] - 2026-10-27

**The weekly release accepts a commit a green train merged, and five lane frictions seen in operation are gone.** Trains merge faster than the main backstop settles, so most main commits ended with a neutral (`superseded`) `main-backstop` check run and the weekly cut returned `NO_GREEN_COMMIT` for a week of commits every one of which merged through a green train. The evidence already existed in `refs/notes/gstack-trains`; the gate now reads it. Alongside: `gstack-issue-links` no longer turns another repository's `(name #N, #M)` into this repository's Refs lines, `gstack-post` no longer asks for a confirmation on run ids written next to run words, `gstack-post pr-body` no longer wipes a PR body when a lane posts one section, and `gstack-ship-queue ready` finds the pregate verdict a lane recorded from a separate clone.

### Changed
- **`scripts/release-cut.ts`**: a commit on main's first-parent history is gated either by a successful backstop check run or by a train record (kind `train`, state `green`, `merging` or `merged`) whose `merged[]` lists its sha or its tree, the main commits `gstack-ship-queue verify --train` confirmed. Everything else stays required: the required check run succeeded, no red check run (a red backstop on a covered commit still refuses), nothing still running, no active freeze. A commit with neither is refused with the same message as before. The `CANDIDATE` line says `gated by main-backstop` or `gated by train <nonce>`. The notes ref is fetched and read once (`readTrainNotes`: the freeze and the train evidence together; `activeFreeze` is folded into it). New flags `--required-check <name>` (default `free-tests`), `--backstop-check <name>` (default `main-backstop`) and `--notes-ref <ref>` (default `refs/notes/gstack-trains`) let another repository run the script; `weekly-release.yml` is unchanged.
- **`lib/issue-links.ts`**: a parenthesised named reference, `(name #N[, #M]…)`, `(name PR #N)` or `(name issue #N)`, where the name is one token that is not a closure, reference, filler or version word (fix, fixes, fixing, closes, closing, resolves, addresses, implements, supersedes, refs, see, related, part, follow-up, deferred, PR, issue, bug, upstream, cf., e.g., i.e., of, to, the, v1.2, …), is a cross-repo reference to `name` (`Refs name#N`), never a same-repo Refs line or a `fix #N` promotion candidate. `(see #12)`, `(closing #12)`, `(cf. #12)`, `(#301)` and `Fixes #12` keep their meaning; the `owner/repo#N` form is unchanged.
- **`lib/gstack-post.ts`**: an 11-digit GitHub Actions run id right after a run word on the same line (run, runs, screen, screens, gate, gates, backstop, bisect, rerun, dispatched, dispatch, failed, passed, with an optional `:` `#` `=`; a generic word such as id, job, attempt or workflow exempts nothing), and every id chained after an allowlisted one through `, `, ` and `, ` & `, ` or ` or ` / ` (a `(#1234)` between allowed), is exempt from `pii.phone.e164`. `failed 40269992077 | rerun passed 40287239206`, `screen 40269992077 (#3434) and 40275443393 (#3453)` and `gate 40323989742` post without `--confirm`. A bare 11-digit number, a 10-digit national number and `+14155551234` still report.
- **`lib/gstack-post.ts`** (`pr-body`): the body file is merged by `## ` section into the PR's current body (read with `gh pr view --json body`, or `glab mr view`, through the same runner) instead of replacing it. A section in the file replaces the same-titled section in place (case-insensitive), the ````gstack-ship-receipt```` block is a section of its own so a receipt rewrite replaces only the receipt, sections the file does not rewrite are kept byte for byte, new sections are appended after them, and a current body with no `## ` headings is kept as the leading text. A `## ` line inside a code fence is not a section: a fence closes only on a run of its own character at least as long as the opener with nothing after it, so a ``` line inside a ```` block or a ```js line closes nothing, and a receipt fence that never closes is an unclosed fence (the body after it stays one kept section) rather than a receipt that swallows `## Approvals`. The file's leading text replaces the current leading text; text after a receipt block never replaces an intro; whitespace-only text in the file is dropped, so reposting the body /ship composes (receipt, blank line, sections) is byte-stable. One stderr line names the replaced, kept and added sections. `--replace` keeps the plain overwrite for a caller that composed the whole body. The redaction scan and the confirmation token cover the merged bytes, which are the bytes sent. A current body that cannot be read posts nothing (exit 3) and names `--replace`.
- **`lib/pregate/index.ts`**, **`lib/ship-queue.ts`**: `gstack-pregate` mirrors every record it writes to `<state root>/pregate/by-tree/<tree>.json` (best effort; a mirror failure never fails the record). `ready` reads the checkout's `.gstack/tmp/pregate.json` (or `--pregate`) first; when it is missing, unreadable, recorded for another tree, or current but still waiting on a remote receipt, it looks the current tree up in the mirror and uses that record when it verifies, printing `PREGATE: … (from the state root's pregate/by-tree/<tree12>.json, recorded by another checkout)`. A lane whose `gstack-pregate --remote` had to run in a separate clone (a worktree cannot host it) no longer gets `PREGATE_STALE`, `PREGATE_REMOTE_UNCLEARED` or `missing` from its own checkout. Only a run that holds the tests stage stands in (what `--stage tests --remote` writes): a mirror without the `lanes` check (an `--only timing` or preflight-only run), one recorded against another base, or one run under `--policy-from head` is named on the `PREGATE:` line and never certifies READY; a record whose own checks failed or stayed incomplete is never overridden. A mirror for another tree changes nothing; the mirror is written through a temp file and rename.

### Docs
- `docs/releases.md`: the release-gate paragraph describes both kinds of evidence, what train evidence does not relax, the `CANDIDATE` wording and the three flags. `docs/pregate.md`: the by-tree mirror and how `ready` reads it.
- `docs/troubleshooting.md`: `#redact-run-id-as-phone` (what triggers `pii.phone.e164` on a receipt token or a run id, the positions `gstack-post` allowlists, and the fix), `#gstack-post-pr-body-merge` (what `pr-body` keeps, replaces and adds, and `--replace`) and `#gate-error-no-base` (`GATE_ERROR=no_base` from `gstack-gate-diff`, the printed fetch command, and `SCOPE_ERROR=no_base` from `gstack-diff-scope` for the same cause).

### Tests
- `test/release-cut.test.ts`: on the real bare origin with train records pushed to `refs/notes/gstack-trains`, a neutral backstop plus a record naming the sha, or only the tree, is the candidate and the `CANDIDATE` line names the train; a covered commit is still refused by a red check run, a red backstop, a missing or failed required run, a running run, and a record in state `red`, `superseded`, `incomplete` or `free-green` is not evidence; with no record every neutral commit is skipped with the unchanged text and an older covered commit wins; the three flags rename what the gate reads through `planRelease` and the CLI, and the defaults do not see a record under another ref.
- `test/ship-issue-intent.test.ts`: `(gbrain #7625, #7606)`, `(gbrain PR #7630)` and `(acme/tools issue #4)` are cross references with no Refs line and no promotion candidate; `(see #12)`, `(fixes #12)`, `(PR #12)` and the other reference words stay bare refs; `(#301)` and `Fixes #12` are unchanged.
- `test/gstack-post.test.ts`: each run-word and chained shape posts; the id without a run word, an id after `see`, a 10-digit number, `+14155551234` and `run +14155551234` still need confirmation. For `pr-body`, through `runPost` with a fake runner answering `gh pr view --json body`: a first-section-only file keeps the receipt and the other sections and the stderr line names them; a same-titled section is replaced in place; a receipt-only file replaces only the receipt; new sections are appended; a `## ` inside a code fence is not a heading; `--replace` overwrites without reading the body; a headingless current body is kept as the leading text; an empty current body posts the file byte for byte; a secret in a kept section is a HIGH refusal on the merged bytes; a failed read is exit 3 with the `--replace` hint; `--replace` on another operation is a usage error.
- `test/gstack-ship-queue.test.ts`: a mirror for the current tree under `GSTACK_STATE_ROOT` makes `ready` pass from a stale `--pregate` and from a missing default file, with the `from` suffix; a mirror for another tree leaves `PREGATE_STALE` and `missing` as they were; a current explicit `--pregate` is used as before with no suffix.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, rubric, trial count, case kind or judge prompt changed. The release gate accepts a new kind of evidence (a green, merging or merged train record naming the commit) and relaxes no other requirement; the `gstack-post` allowlist widens only for 11-digit tokens in the listed positions.

## [1.91.261.0] - 2026-10-27

**`gstack-restamp --next` moves a PR's quoted `since:` rows when its VERSION already equals the base's (gbrain #7640).** A gbrain PR stamped 0.60.468.0, lost its slot, merged master, and master was 0.60.468.0 by then. At its next slot restamp left the PR's `{ since: '0.60.468.0', … }` notice rows at .468 while the release shipped as .469, and gbrain's `compareReleases` then hid that notice from every user already on .468. Two gaps combined: with VERSION equal on both sides the branch had no stamp of its own, so nothing was rewritten everywhere, and the mention scanner that reads the lines the branch added could not pass the opening quote of a quoted row (`since:\s*(\d…)`), so it found nothing either. `--was 0.60.468.0` was no answer, because it rewrites master's own .468 rows too. The quote fix alone covers that merged-base state (the base's .468 is newer than the branch's .467 fork point, so the scanner names it); the equal-version rule below covers the state the fork-point floor cannot, a branch rebased onto the base after it reached X, or one never stamped.

### Fixed
- **Quoted versions are stamp forms** in both the mention scanner (`tentativeMentions`) and the exact rewrite table (`rewriteStamps`) of `lib/restamp.ts`: `since: 'X'`, `since: "X"`, `(was 'X')` and `(was "X")` match like the bare forms and keep their quote style, and an opened quote must close right after X, so `since: '1.2.3-beta'` and a mismatched `since: '1.2.3"` are not the form (the tree receipt and the gate-reuse normalizers share `rewriteStamps`, so a quoted `since:` rewrite classifies as a stamp without a template, and a quoted prerelease change never does); `vX` already accepted a quote before the `v`. The scanner also reads the policy's `stamp_patterns` templates, so a template-only form on a branch-added line is a candidate too.
- **The equal-version rule.** When the branch has no stamp of its own (its VERSION equals the base's and no `--was` is given), a stamp-form mention of the base version on a line the branch added is its stale tentative stamp and moves to the allocated version; the same version on a line the base already carries is the base's release and stays. The `stamp_paths` stage detail, printed in the stage table and kept in the journal, names both counts per file (`VERSION equals base X, so X moved only on lines this branch added and stayed on the base's own lines (<file>: N moved, M kept)`), so the stamp commit's tool output shows which lines moved and why; when an explicit stamp matched nothing the skipped detail now names the version it searched for. The rule reads line ownership, not meaning: a branch-added `Requires vX or later` inside `stamp_paths` on a branch forked at X moves too, visible in `--dry-run` and the counts; `docs/ship-policy.md` says how to write such a reference. The explicit `--was X` path is unchanged and still rewrites X on every line; its help line now says so and names the CHANGELOG re-heading it also drives.
- **Branch-added lines are known by position, not text.** `branchAddedLines` records each added line's new-side position beside its text (`parseUnifiedDiff` counts it through any context line a hunk carries, and the diff pins `--inter-hunk-context=0` so a `diff.interHunkContext` setting cannot join hunks), and the stage rewrites by position, so a base line whose text equals a branch-added line stays while the added copy moves, and a CRLF checkout (`core.autocrlf`, `eol=crlf`), whose diff is LF-normalized while the file carries CR, still finds the branch's row instead of reporting `0 moved` and shipping it stale.
- **A stamp interrupted after VERSION was written retries as a stamp.** The journal recovery restored the branch's own stamp but kept the already-written VERSION as a stamp when the original was the base version, so the retry rewrote nothing and returned `noop` with the row still stale; it now restores the equal-base provenance (no branch stamp) and the retry completes the stamp.

### Tests
- `test/restamp-mentions.test.ts`: the pure forms (single quote, double quote, bare unchanged, quote style kept, a mismatched quote pair refused, a template overlapping the built-in form counted once, the fork-version floor on quoted mentions) and, on the fixture repo, the reporter's state rebuilt with the real `bin/gstack-restamp`: the other PR takes the slot through the tool, the PR merges main with VERSION equal on both sides, and `--next` moves the PR's quoted row, keeps the base's two rows byte for byte, and says why in the stage detail; the same with the built-in form alone (no `since:` template); a negative control where the PR adds no base-version mention and every base-side quoted row stays; a branch forked at the base version (fork equals base, nothing stamped) whose own base-version row and doc mention move while the base's stay; and `--was` rewriting the base's row as well; then the quoted-prerelease and mismatched-quote boundaries in both the scanner and the table, a branch-added line whose text equals a base line (the base copy stays), a CRLF checkout, and an apply interrupted by `EACCES` after VERSION was written whose retry completes the stamp. Eleven of the file's thirteen cases are red at 1.91.253.0 (the template-overlap and `--was` cases pass there, as they should).
- `test/stamp-templates.test.ts`: the quoted `since:` row now counts once with or without the template (it pinned zero without one).

### Docs
- `docs/ship-policy.md`: the `stamp_paths` stage states the quoted forms and the provenance rule (the branch's own stamp everywhere; on branch-added lines, mentions newer than the fork version and, with VERSION equal to the base's, the base version; `--was` as the rewrite-everywhere tool).
