It runs `bin/gstack-design-craft` on each page's served HTML (or the repo file when no app runs) and files each `CRAFT_CHECK` line as a category 9 finding (no `CRAFT_RESULT` line means the check was unavailable, and a framework mount-node shell is judged by eye too; the saved page holds only inline CSS and JS, so `100vh`, `transition: all`, scroll listeners and `alert()` are also judged by eye; it also holds session data, so it is deleted in the block that checks it, whatever the exit code, and never copied to the report; `--accepted` takes that screen's finalized.json, only for a page /design-html finalized, and never covers `needs-proof` or `lorem`; a claim without proof is filed and asked about, never marked or cut); checks what the tool cannot see (claims only from the user, realistic sample content, the ship floor, a designed 404, cookie consent where required, the motion rules); files a failed Persuade check (one primary action, named objections, proof beside each claim, a real risk reversal, an index/noindex decision) as a deferred High finding, since its fix needs the team's copy or indexing call; and in Phase 8 breaks impact ties with Elaya's fix order and reads the installed Tailwind major version before touching its config. ## [1.91.259.0] - 2026-10-26

**New `/ubicloud` skill: the Ubicloud runner moves into gstack with the discipline a shared vCPU quota needs.** Crews ran heavy suites on Ubicloud through a user-scope skill and per-lane wrappers, and paid for it in stray VMs after a machine slept, a project quota at 528 of 512 vCPUs when lanes verified in parallel, verifies that hung for an hour before anyone noticed, and a stale wrapper that skipped a service start. `scripts/ubicloud/ubi-runner.sh` now carries the fixes and `ubicloud/SKILL.md` (entry point `bin/gstack-ubi`) teaches the watched launch; `bun run test:ubicloud` and the remote pregate are unchanged.

### Added
- **`ubicloud/SKILL.md.tmpl`, `bin/gstack-ubi`**: the skill: set/unset prerequisite checks (never `env`), `UBI_OWNER` on every machine, a watched launch (a waited-on background operation or `gstack-detach`), the quoted recovery line, one committed verify per repository, how to read exit 124 and a quota refusal, and the resume checklist. Classified `CLAUDE_ONLY` in `lib/doctor-components.ts`; routed from the root `SKILL.md`; listed in README, AGENTS.md, docs/skills.md and docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md.
- **TTL names and a reaper**: a generated VM name ends in `-t<hours>` (`UBI_TTL_HOURS`, default 4; 0 omits it). `reap` destroys every VM in the project whose TTL ended more than ten minutes ago, whichever owner created it, and every `up` runs it first (`UBI_REAP=0` skips it). Names without a TTL, including the ones `pregate-remote.sh` builds, are never reaped.
- **Quota preflight**: `up` adds the size's vCPUs to the project's running VMs and refuses before the create request when that exceeds the known ceiling (`UBI_QUOTA_VCPUS`, or the maximum the last API refusal printed, remembered in the state root); `UBI_QUOTA_WAIT=<seconds>` polls for room instead of refusing. Both refusals (the preflight's and the API's) print the per-owner `usage` table.
- **Watchdog and heartbeat**: `run`, `verify` and `ssh NAME COMMAND` stream the remote output (both streams kept in the VM's state dir) through a watchdog: a heartbeat every `UBI_HEARTBEAT` seconds (300), and a command silent for `UBI_IDLE_TIMEOUT` seconds (1800) or older than `UBI_RUN_TIMEOUT` (0, unlimited) is killed in its own session with exit 124 and its last 40 lines on stderr. `run` also prints the VM's TTL and its `down` recovery command as soon as the VM is ready.
- **`verify`**: runs the repository's committed `.gstack/ubicloud.json` (setup, command, size, location, storage, image, env, pass, pull; flags and a trailing `-- COMMAND` override it) and refuses without the file or a command, so every lane runs one definition instead of its own wrapper. The file is repository content and gets no reach beyond the checkout: `setup` and each `pull` destination must be relative paths that resolve inside `--src` (absolute, `~` and `..` paths are refused before any API call, and under `verify` every pull destination is resolved again, symlinks followed, right before its pull, so a symlink an earlier pull planted cannot redirect a later one; a refused pull makes the run exit 1), and a name under `pass` is forwarded only when the command line grants it (`--pass NAME`, or every listed name with `--trust-config`; `verify` parses its options by arity, so an option value can never act as that flag). `--pass` never forwards `UBICLOUD_*`, from the file or the command line.
- **Watched commands keep their stdin and exit codes**: `ssh NAME COMMAND` hands the caller's stdin to the remote command (`printf payload | gstack-ubi ssh NAME 'cat > file'` wrote an empty file once the watchdog backgrounded the client), a command that finished while the watchdog read the clock, or in the instant before its kill, keeps its own exit status instead of 124, a hung setup script exits 124 like a hung command instead of 1, Ctrl-C on a watched command takes the ssh session down with it, and when the watchdog fires the runner also ends the command's session on the VM (`setsid` there, leader pid in `~/.ubirun-<phase>-<runner pid>.sid`, kept until the cancel reads it so a background child the command left behind is still reachable, `pkill -s` bounded to 20 s), since killing the local client alone leaves a silent remote command running until it next writes.
- **`pack` and `sync` from a linked worktree**: a worktree's `.git` is a one-line pointer into the main repository, so the VM got a checkout whose git did not work (`gstack-pregate --remote` from a Capy worktree failed with `PREGATE_VM_TREE_MISMATCH vm=unavailable`). The tarball now carries a self-contained clone of the checked-out branch with the worktree's own index in its place (about 45 MB for gstack instead of the main repository's full `.git`); a detached worktree is refused with the fix named.
- **Quota ceiling and reaper outcomes**: the maximum a refusal cached is trusted for a day, then the API's own answer decides again; the refusal line says where the ceiling came from and names `UBI_QUOTA_VCPUS`, and its `vCPU quota exhausted` wording is the one `pregate-remote.sh` retries once on. `reap` returns 1 when the list fails (nothing destroyed) or an expired VM could not be destroyed, instead of 0 either way; a TTL suffix is read in base 10 (`UBI_TTL_HOURS` takes 0 to 999 with no leading zero).

### Tests
- `test/ubicloud-runner.test.ts`: against the fake API, `up` reaps an expired other-owner VM, names its own VM `-t4`, and the preflight refuses with no create call; `UBI_REAP=0` and `UBI_TTL_HOURS=0`; `reap` leaves unexpired and TTL-less names alone. Against a fake `ssh`, the watchdog returns 124 with the last output and the heartbeat line appears. `verify` refuses a missing file, a missing command, a missing setup script (resolved against `--src`) and invalid JSON, all before any API call. A second fixture whose fake API can create runs `run` end to end: a hung setup exits 124 and still destroys the VM, `UBI_RUN_TIMEOUT` kills a chatty command, `--pass` writes the named variable (and never `UBICLOUD_*` or a non-name) into the VM's env file without printing it, `ssh NAME COMMAND` passes stdin through, `verify` refuses ungranted `pass` names and setup or pull paths outside `--src` and runs once granted, a quota refusal caches its maximum which drives the preflight until it is a day old, `UBI_QUOTA_WAIT` waits before refusing, and `reap` reports a failed list or destroy.
- `test/catalog-budget.test.ts` ratchet 1,251 → 1,289 token-equivalents (ubicloud adds 150 bytes on top of /captain's 1,251); `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` gains the `ubicloud` ceiling only.

## [1.91.258.0] - 2026-10-26

**The session check stops failing for things that are not failures, and a consuming repository can name the gstack it wants without broadcasting to every thread.** Five Captains running gstack on Capy hit the same install friction this week: eight crew-wide "upgrade to <version>" messages since Oct 16, `gstack: fail not-installed` on coordinator machines that run no workflow, `fail pins` from the image's Node while the tests run on the pinned one, reviewers told to "reinstall" when asked to run a workflow, and an environment dump from a broken `/cso` shell line. Each of these is now a product behaviour instead of a crew rule.

### Added
- **Project floor** (`floor` row in `gstack-doctor --check`, `lib/doctor-components.ts`, `bin/gstack-doctor-check.sh`): a consuming repository declares the oldest gstack it wants its crew on as `min_gstack_version` in its `.gstack/ship-policy.json` (the field `gstack-ship-queue` already validates; a file holding only that field is valid). The doctor reads it from the project the check runs in: `PASS floor <f> declared by <file>`, `SKIP floor (... declares none)`, or `WARN floor — installed <v> is below the floor <f> ...; fix: <install command>` (`PROJECT_FLOOR_UNMET`). The Capy installer adds `floor=<f> (<file>)` and a `fix:` note to its ok trailer. One commit in the project replaces a message to every thread; the fix on Capy is the install command, which fast-forwards a clean checkout to origin in one step.
- **`--for none`** (`capy/skill/gstack/scripts/install.sh` wrapper 3, `bin/gstack-capy-install`): a machine that runs no gstack workflow (a coordinator, a liaison, a Captain) prints `gstack: ok not-needed for=none (<notes>)` and exits 0, installing, moving and certifying nothing, with or without a checkout. The bootstrapper answers it itself, so the line is honest for any checkout revision. That ok admits no workflow: no install verdict is written, so a workflow started there is refused with the usual `--for <skill>` fix. `GSTACK_CAPY_MIN_WRAPPER` is 3; older Drive copies keep working and print the owner action.
- **Review-voice machines upgrade in place** (`bin/gstack-capy-install`): running `--for <skill>` on a machine installed `--for review-voice` says `upgrading the review-voice install in place to --for <skill> (same checkout ...; no second clone)`, applies the project's pins, runs `./setup` and both host profiles, and writes the workflow's verdict over the reviewer's. The admission refusal's fix now says so (`upgrades this checkout in place: ./setup and host profiles, no second clone`) instead of reading like a reinstall.

### Changed
- **A gap above the supported minimum is never a hard fail** (`bin/gstack-capy-install`): an install-mode session whose session-start fast-forward was skipped (dirty, diverged or pinned checkout, a live lease, `gstack-upgrade` missing) prints `WARN behind — ... and the session-start upgrade was skipped: <reason>; fix: <command> (UPGRADE_BUSY|UPGRADE_REFUSED|UPGRADE_SKIPPED)` and keeps its ok trailer with `behind=<n> (latest: <ver>); upgrade skipped: <reason> (<CODE>); fix: <command>` notes, exit 0. It used to be `gstack: fail behind`, exit 1. Below the supported minimum the bootstrapper still fails `revision` (`REVISION_BELOW_MINIMUM`).
- **A Node-only pin mismatch is advisory** (`bin/gstack-doctor-check.sh`): when the project's Node pin is unmet by the Node on PATH while every Bun pin is met, `pins` is `WARN pins — ... (node pin only; bun pins pass); fix: ... (PROJECT_NODE_PIN_UNMET)` and the trailer stays ok. gstack runs on Bun and the project's tests choose their Node (nvm, the CI matrix). A Bun pin that is unmet stays `FAIL pins` (`PROJECT_PIN_MISMATCH`).
- **WARN rows print their action as given** (`_dc_row`): `owner action: ...` for the Capy skill copy, `fix: ...` for the floor, a skipped upgrade and a Node pin, so a lane knows which WARNs it can clear itself.
- **A Drive copy below the wrapper minimum is a WARN in a direct run too** (`bin/gstack-doctor-check.sh`): with no bootstrapper provenance (`bin/gstack-upgrade`'s installer run, a direct `gstack-doctor --check`), every Drive copy at a bootstrapper revision below `GSTACK_CAPY_MIN_WRAPPER` is `WARN wrapper — every Capy skill copy is below the minimum wrapper 3 (it still works): ...` with the owner action and an ok trailer; only a pre-bootstrapper copy (no `GSTACK_CAPY_WRAPPER=` line) still fails. Found by /ship's red team: raising the minimum to 3 would otherwise have failed every direct run on a machine whose Drive copy is the deployed wrapper 2 until the owner recopied the skill.
- **A `--for none` session never self-upgrades** (`bin/gstack-capy-session`): an older bootstrapper (wrapper 1 or 2) hands `--for none` to the session in install mode; the session now treats it like `--check` (reports `behind=`, moves nothing) before the installer prints `ok not-needed`; the old bootstrapper's own clone or fast-forward of a below-minimum checkout, before the handover, is unchanged. Wrapper 3 answers `--for none` before the session. The session's header comment describes the `WARN behind` outcome (it said `fail behind`).
- **/cso** (`cso/SKILL.md.tmpl`): the always-loaded startup block gains two rules. Environment hygiene: prerequisite checks read a variable as set or unset only, and `env`, `printenv`, `set -x`, a bare `set` or `export`, `export $(...)` and `echo "$NAME"` never appear in a tool fence. Tooling errors fail loudly: a non-zero exit with no helper status is retried at most twice (5 s, 30 s; `start` is resumed, not restarted, because a run may exist before its ID prints) and then ends **not assessed** for whatever the helper never recorded, quoting the command, exit code and stderr tail; never a quiet partial, never another review offered as the missing coverage.
- **Capy skill and docs** (`capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md`, `docs/capy-install.md`): the session-start steps cover `--for none`, `floor=`, `behind=` as informational, the Node WARN and the in-place review-voice upgrade; run directories and scratch on Capy live under `~/.capy/work/<name>`, never `/tmp`, which Capy wipes when a machine sleeps.
- **Result codes** (`lib/result-codes-capy.ts`): `PROJECT_FLOOR_UNMET`, `PROJECT_NODE_PIN_UNMET` and `UPGRADE_SKIPPED`, each with a `docs/troubleshooting.md` anchor.
- **The trailer's `fix:` after a skipped upgrade is one runnable command** (`bin/gstack-capy-install`): the session's rerun or `bin/gstack-upgrade` (which prints its own refusal), never the refusal's prose; that prose, with its `GSTACK_UPGRADE_FORCE=1` escape hatch for a live lease, stays on the `WARN behind` row (found by /ship's adversarial review: an agent told to run the `fix:` command was being handed prose with the note separator in it).
- **The floor reader is whitespace-insensitive** (`bin/gstack-doctor-check.sh`): `min_gstack_version` on one line and its value on the next, which `lib/ship-policy.ts` accepts, is read, the first occurrence (the top-level field) wins, only the first 64 KiB of the file are read, and a present string value that is not a plain dotted version SKIPs as such instead of as "null or absent" (found by Codex and the adversarial pass in /ship's review).

### Tests
- `test/gstack-doctor.test.ts`: the `floor` row's four outcomes (absent file, null key, met, unmet with the wrapper fix and without it) and the Node-only WARN beside a Bun-plus-Node FAIL; every required-row list gains `floor`.
- `test/gstack-capy-install.test.ts`: a skipped session-start upgrade is an ok trailer with the `upgrade skipped` note and a `WARN behind` row (replacing the `fail behind` pin); a `WARN floor` row becomes the `floor=` and `fix:` notes, with one `fix:` when `behind=` is also present; `--for none` with and without a checkout; a review-voice verdict upgraded in place by `--for autoplan` (setup runs, the verdict becomes the workflow's).
- `test/capy-skill-wrapper.test.ts`: `--for none` through the bootstrapper (checkout present, install mode, no checkout), wrapper 3 in the handover; a wrapper-2 handover of `--for none` in install mode leaves HEAD where it was.
- `test/gstack-doctor.test.ts`: a direct run with every Drive copy a bootstrapper below the minimum is a WARN with an ok trailer, and a pre-bootstrapper copy beside it keeps the FAIL. `test/gstack-capy-install.test.ts`: an unknown skip code collapses to `UPGRADE_SKIPPED` with its anchor; the in-place upgrade message is silent for a same-profile rerun, `--check` and a second review-voice install.
- `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts`: the /cso skeleton pin moves to 18,900 (measured 18,843) for the two startup paragraphs; `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` pins `capy/skill/gstack` and `cso` at their new eager sizes.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, rubric, trial count, case kind or judge prompt changed. The /cso skeleton cap and two context-budget ceilings went up by the measured size of the added prose, with the reason in the pin.

## [1.91.257.0] - 2026-10-26

**A remote gate that ran ahead of the stamp now clears /ship's small-machine obligation; gbrain stops paying a second full gate per PR.** `gstack-pregate clear --remote pregate.json/remote_gate --receipt <file>` accepts a `PREGATE_REMOTE:` receipt whose tree differs from pregate.json's tree only in the repo's declared stamp paths. gstack proves it itself: a `git diff` of the two trees, every differing file classified by the tree receipt's own rule (`lib/tree-receipt.ts` `classifyFile` under `.gstack/ship-policy.json` on the base branch: `stamp_files`, `stamp_patterns`, and the built-in version-file, manifest-version, lockfile-root-version and changelog-heading forms), so the pregate verdict and `gstack-tree-receipt`'s can never disagree; there is no second stamp list, and its gate rule holds too: a policy whose `stamp_sensitive_gates` names the test lane (`tests`, as gstack's own policy does) refuses the substitution, because the tree receipt never marks that lane reusable. The policy is the ship's own base branch's (`origin/HEAD`); a pregate.json recorded against another base is refused. gbrain's rule lets a head reuse a full gate whose tree differs only in release stamps, but /ship's Step 12 restamp always changed those files, so no gate-ahead run could satisfy `remote_gate` and every gbrain PR ran the whole gate again after /ship (#7621, #7674, #7681: 17–37 min, 64–128 vCPU each).

### Added
- **`lib/pregate/remote-receipt.ts`** (`substituteStampOnlyTree`): both trees must be objects here (the gated commit fetched, the head tree `bin/gstack-wtree` wrote); a path outside the rule, a stamp path whose hunk is not the exact old → new rewrite, an unfetched or non-hex gated tree, an unreadable, unfetched or invalid base policy, a policy whose `stamp_sensitive_gates` names the test lane, a pregate.json recorded against another base, a patch that does not account for every path `git diff-tree` lists, or a `stamp_files` hunk between two trees at the same version refuse with `PREGATE_RECEIPT_INVALID` and a fix naming the offending path (`lib/x.ts (stamp_files: not in the repo's stamp_files allowlist, line 1)`). The patch is read with a fixed presentation (`--no-textconv --no-renames --ignore-submodules=none`, `a/` `b/` prefixes) so a diff driver or `diff.*` setting can neither hide nor rename a path. The receipt's tests and failed checks are unchanged and run before any git work.
- **The substitution is recorded.** The receipt string gains `accepted-for=<head> stamp-only=<n>` after `tests=`, and pregate.json's obligation carries `substitution: { gated_tree, accepted_for, policy, files: [{ path, rule }] }`; `clear` prints `PREGATE_RECEIPT_SUBSTITUTED: gated tree … accepted for tree … under <policy>; stamp-only: <path> (<rule>), …`, `verify` repeats it on its ok line, and a substitution whose `accepted_for` is not pregate.json's tree, or whose `gated_tree` is not the receipt string's `tree=`, is `PREGATE_REMOTE_UNCLEARED`.
- **Docs:** [docs/pregate.md#remote-gate-stamp-only](docs/pregate.md#remote-gate-stamp-only) (what is accepted, what is refused, how a consuming repo declares its stamp paths: `.gstack/ship-policy.json` on the base branch, the file the tree receipt already reads, and the four-command sequence that reuses a gate-ahead run); the `PREGATE_RECEIPT_INVALID` and `PREGATE_REMOTE_UNCLEARED` troubleshooting anchors.

### Changed
- `lib/tree-receipt.ts` exports `classifyFile` (the function is unchanged) so pregate reuses the rule instead of restating it; `PregateRemote` in `lib/headless-artifacts.ts` gains the optional `substitution` field (`PregateReceiptSubstitution`) and its schema entry. Both trees must be 40- or 64-hex object ids before any git call (a symbolic `HEAD^{tree}` in a receipt is refused, never recorded as the gated tree), and `clearDecision` now takes the repository root.

### Tests
- `test/pregate-remote-stamp-only.test.ts`: accept (five stamp files under a `stamp_files` + `stamp_patterns` policy, the recorded substitution equal to `gstack-tree-receipt`'s file verdicts on the same pair, `verify` ok), the unchanged same-tree path, refusals (a path outside the rule, a stamp path with a description edit, an unfetched gated tree, an unreadable receipt file, zero tests, a failure, a symbolic tree, a head tree not in the object store, a mode-only difference, a stamp file at the wrong version, a pregate.json recorded against another base with and without origin/HEAD, an invalid base policy, a policy whose `stamp_sensitive_gates` names the test lane), `verify` on a misapplied substitution, and a same-tree re-clear dropping the recorded substitution.

## [1.91.256.0] - 2026-10-26

**The /ship review loop converges, and a receipt survives a base merge.** Five Captains' /ship runs hit the review cap on the same PR shape: every pass re-reviewed the whole diff, reviewers answered an empty range with an invented advisory, and each advisory earned another full pass; four more re-ran /ship on product code they had not changed because a conflict-only main merge or a test fix moved the head the receipt named. The loop now fixes blocking findings in the diff on pass 1, reads only the range since the previous pass afterwards, caps at three passes, and counts `passes=<n> blocking_found=<k> deferred=<m>` in the ship receipt; the receipt carries to the new head when the product patch-id is unchanged. The blocking floor is the owner's call (Garry, 2026-10-26: "Ok set it at that"), and the policy lives in gstack rather than in any one team's rules (Garry, 2026-10-26: "Gstack should be the actual holder of how to do things not one off Capy files"): `docs/review-policy.md` is the canonical statement, the skills carry it as their written policy, and a crew rule can be one line pointing at it.

### Added
- **`docs/review-policy.md`**: the canonical review policy: the blocking floor, `NO FINDINGS` as a result, how `/ship` converges (pass 1 the diff, pass 2+ the range, three passes), what the receipt's `review_loop` records, the `review_scope` table and where each rule is enforced. `ship/SKILL.md` states it in a Review policy paragraph in the always-loaded skeleton and `review/SKILL.md` Step 4 states the floor and the `NO FINDINGS` rule beside the checklist order, each pointing at the doc.
- **`lib/review-scope.ts`, `bin/gstack-review-scope`** (`classify`, `defer`, `render`, `summary`): each finding gets a `locus` (`diff`, `fix-range`, `outside`; a hunk plus three context lines), a `kind`, `blocking` (a CRITICAL defect: a test that would fail, a production break, a security or data-loss defect) and a `scope`: `fix`, `defer` (a blocking finding in code the PR did not change, filed as a GitHub issue reused through a `<!-- gstack-deferred-finding: <fingerprint> -->` marker, `unfiled (<reason>)` without `gh`) or `note`. `render` writes the PR body's `## Deferred findings` and `## Review notes` sections; `summary --since <REVIEW_SINCE>` reads this invocation's review-log rows into the receipt's `review_loop` counters. Refusals end in `REVIEW_SCOPE_INPUT` or `REVIEW_SCOPE_RANGE`.
- **`.gstack/ship-policy.json` `review_scope`** (`frozen` | `diff-plus-blocking` | `all`, default `frozen`, since 1.91.249.0; a non-default value needs `min_gstack_version`): the blocking floor is owner-approved (Garry, 2026-10-26: "Ok set it at that"); `diff-plus-blocking` is the documented fallback that fixes a blocking finding in unchanged code in this PR instead of filing it, and `all` is the earlier loop, every finding fixed on every pass. `show-effective` prints the choice as a `ship: review_scope …` line ([docs/ship-policy.md#review-scope](docs/ship-policy.md#review-scope)).
- **`gstack-ship-receipt carry (--pr <n> | --body <file>) --base <base> [--dry-run] [--json]`**: moves the receipt to HEAD when the receipt head is an ancestor of HEAD and the product diff against the base has the same `git patch-id` at both heads; tests (`CARRY_TEST_GLOBS`), release metadata (`CARRY_METADATA_GLOBS`) and the base merge's own commits may differ. The carried receipt records `carry: { from, reason, product_patch_id, changed_paths, merge_commits, range_diff, covers, reruns }`, prints `CARRY: carried from <old> to <new> (<reason>)` and the `GSTACK_RESULT` line, and its summary line ends `carried_from=<old12>`. A product change is `RECEIPT_CARRY_PRODUCT_CHANGED` (exit 3, naming the paths); a rebased or missing receipt is `RECEIPT_CARRY_REFUSED`. `write` takes `--review-loop <json|@file>`; `ShipReceipt` gains optional `review_loop` and `carry` with schema ([docs/ship-policy.md#receipt-carry](docs/ship-policy.md#receipt-carry), [docs/unattended.md](docs/unattended.md#the-terminal-line)).
- **Severity glossary and lead judgment** (ideas absorbed from tstack's sol-loop and pstack's interrogate, rewritten; NOTICE.md): `docs/review-policy.md`, `ship/sections/review-army.md` Step 9.4 and `review/checklist.md` budget the loop by three words (a **blocker** is the intended case gone wrong, the floor; a **should** is a real bug a caller will hit inside the intended case, fixed in the diff on pass 1 and deferred otherwise; a **nit** is the rest, a named note) and carry two stop rules (fixes that grew the diff past the request are cut first; the cap approves nothing, so a standing blocker is reported). The finding merge both /review and /ship render (`scripts/resolvers/review-army.ts`) gains stage 4, lead judgment: nit gravity, hypothetical versus actual, structure for a case nothing takes, a different design is not a defect, missing context; independent agreement is the strongest signal and a reviewer's `NO FINDINGS` stands until a traced defect says otherwise. Every specialist prompt accepts an optional `cause` ({path, line}): a defect the diff causes in code it did not change (a broken caller, a consumer of a removed export) keeps the victim as `path` and the changed line in `cause`, and `classify` follows the anchor, so the finding is the diff's to fix rather than deferred to an issue.

### Changed
- **`ship/sections/review-army.md` Step 9**: first entry saves `REVIEW_SINCE` and the `review_scope` line; every entry saves `PASS_HEAD`, and from pass 2 `RANGE_BASE` is the previous pass's head, so every prompt the step diffs from the merge base (specialists, Red Team, the outside voice in the adversarial section) reads `RANGE_BASE..HEAD` under `frozen`. Step 9.4 item 0 classifies the pass's findings, item 1 queues only `scope: fix`, item 3.5 defers and renders, and the summary line adds `D deferred, O noted`. Decision 2 keeps the three-cycle fix cap and adds the pass cap: a blocking finding still in `fix` scope on pass 3 stops for the owner with the finding named; a pass whose remaining findings are all below the floor applies no edits and ships through decision 4. The review-log row gains `pass`, `review_scope` and `range_base`.
- **Specialist and Red Team prompts** (`scripts/resolvers/review-army.ts`, both /review and /ship): `NO FINDINGS` alone is the expected, complete result for a clean diff and never a failed reviewer; CRITICAL is defined as the blocking floor and everything else is INFORMATIONAL. Shared prose was tightened by the same number of bytes, so /review's generated size is unchanged on every host.
- **`ship/sections/pr-body.md`**: the body carries the `## Deferred findings` and `## Review notes` sections verbatim from `render`, and the receipt write runs after `gstack-review-scope summary`.
- **`ship/SKILL.md` Step 1**: item 4, the carry check, runs `gstack-ship-receipt carry --pr <n> --base <base>` when the branch has an open PR; `CARRY: carried` ends the run with the receipt bound to HEAD.
- **`gstack-ship-receipt carry`, after its own pre-landing review** (two blocking findings reproduced in the QA smoke before the fix): the product patch-id is `git patch-id --verbatim`, so a whitespace-only edit to a reviewed line (`rm -rf "$DIR"/x` → `rm -rf "$DIR" /x`) is a product change; `package.json` and `VERSION` are release metadata only while the from..head change is a version stamp and nothing else (`lib/pregate/stamp-only.ts`), so a dependency, a script or a new key is product; lockfiles left the default metadata list (product unless the policy's `stamp_files`/`stamp_paths` name them); the test globs name code extensions (`**/*.test.ts`, `**/*.spec.rb`, …), so an `openapi.spec.yaml` is product; a working tree with uncommitted changes is `RECEIPT_CARRY_REFUSED` before anything is compared (the carry binds HEAD alone, and a parent that stops at `CARRY: carried` would otherwise report pending edits as shipped); a receipt carried twice keeps the reviewed head as `carry.from` and adds up the hops' merges and paths; the per-path comparison stops at the 20 paths the refusal names and the advisory `git range-diff` gets 15 s; `carry.reruns` says that test and helper code changed since the reviewed head runs in CI unreviewed.
- **`gstack-review-scope`**: `classify` refuses an unresolvable base with `POLICY_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` instead of reading the working tree's policy silently (pass `--policy` to classify without the base), validates `--range-base` as a commit id, runs git with `core.quotePath=false` so a non-ASCII changed path matches its finding, and records `range_base: null` on pass 1; a blocking finding with no path is `fix`, never an issue against `(no path)`; the Testing specialist's `category: testing` is a test finding below the floor (`TEST_GAP_CATEGORIES`), as the policy says; `defer` searches once for every marker before creating anything and files nothing when the search fails (a rate-limited rerun cannot duplicate issues), and exits 0 with `unfiled (<reason>)` lines (the documented degraded path); `summary` refuses with `REVIEW_SCOPE_INPUT` when no via-ship review pass matches `--since`, and `ship/sections/pr-body.md` chains it to the receipt write with `&&` after removing the previous loop file, so a receipt cannot record a loop that did not happen.
- **`ship/sections/review-army.md` pass 2 range**: the core checklist read (item 2) also diffs `$RANGE_BASE` from pass 2 on, as the dispatched prompts already did; the gate scan and the QA probes keep the whole candidate. `docs/review-policy.md` and `docs/ship-policy.md` say so, and name the release that added `review_scope` through `REVIEW_SCOPE_KEY_VERSION` instead of repeating the number.

### Tests
- `test/review-scope.test.ts`: hunk parsing and locus with context, the blocking floor, `fix`/`defer`/`note` on pass 1 and pass 2 with a range base, the `all` policy, deferred-issue reuse through the marker and the unfiled path, the rendered sections and the summary counters.
- `test/gstack-ship-receipt.test.ts`: a base merge and a test-only change carry (receipt names HEAD, `carry` holds the range-diff, the summary line ends `carried_from=`); a product change is `RECEIPT_CARRY_PRODUCT_CHANGED` exit 3 naming the path; a non-ancestor head is `RECEIPT_CARRY_REFUSED`; `--review-loop` lands in the receipt and its summary line.
- `test/gstack-ship-policy.test.ts`: the `ship: review_scope frozen` consequence line, `all` or `diff-plus-blocking` without `min_gstack_version` and an unknown value are `POLICY_INVALID`. `test/review-fix-range.test.ts` asserts the Step 9 prose (PASS_HEAD, RANGE_BASE, classify, the cap rule).
- `test/review-loop-budget-wording.test.ts` (new): the glossary, the stop rules, the lead-judgment stage in both review armies, the `cause` anchor in every specialist prompt, and that `docs/review-policy.md` repeats no version number. `test/review-scope.test.ts`: a non-ASCII changed path classifies as `diff/fix`; `cause` anchors; an unplaced blocking finding is `fix`; `category: testing` is a test gap (asserted against `review/specialists/testing.md`'s schema line); `--pass 0`, `--policy loose`, an option-shaped `--range-base` and a non-array `render --deferred` refuse; an unresolvable base is `POLICY_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`; `defer` lists once, files nothing on a failed search and exits 0 unfiled; `summary` refuses zero passes. `test/gstack-ship-receipt.test.ts`: a whitespace-only edit to a reviewed line and a dirty tree refuse; a lockfile edit and a package.json dependency or script change refuse by path while a version-only stamp carries; a receipt carried twice keeps the reviewed head; the `classifyCarryPath` rows for lockfiles, `.spec.yaml`, stamp-only and non-stamp manifests.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, timeout, trial count or case kind changed. The ship parity `maxSizeRatio` in `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts` moves 1.6740 → 1.7010 (measured 319,071 / 187,706 = 1.6998) and `maxSkeletonBytes` 81,600 → 82,700 (measured 82,645) for Step 1's carry check, Step 9's scope prose and the skeleton's Review policy paragraph. The gstack-review host pins in `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json` go up by 250 characters on all eight pinned hosts (agy, codex, copilot, cursor, factory, kiro, opencode, slate) for the three-line policy statement in Step 4; the resolver prose that renders into those hosts was trimmed by the same number of bytes it gained for the `NO FINDINGS` and floor sentences. Owner decision for the pin raise: Garry, 2026-10-26, "Gstack should be the actual holder of how to do things not one off Capy files".
- Pass-1 review fixes raised the same two caps again, each with its measurement: ship `maxSizeRatio` 1.7010 → 1.7150 (measured 321,630 / 187,706 = 1.7135) for the lead-judgment stage, the `cause` anchor, the glossary, the stop rules and pass 2's core read; review `maxSizeRatio` 1.2960 → 1.3100 (measured 141,949 / 108,523 = 1.3080) for the shared lead-judgment stage and `cause` anchor. The gstack-review pins on the five hosts that inline the review-army section (cursor, factory, kiro, opencode, slate) go up by 1,396 characters each to their exact rendered sizes; agy, codex and copilot carve the section and are unchanged. The owner's standing decision for these raises is the one that opened the lane (GStack Minder, 2026-10-26: the two wording contributions are inside the "too overzealous" ruling, and a cap raise with a stated reason is the lane's to make). `test/review-workflow-clarity.test.ts`'s merge-stage marker list follows the new stage numbering (eight stages; the Red Team reruns 1–8); no assertion was weakened. `test/review-scope.test.ts`'s `defer` expectation moved from exit 3 to exit 0 because the contract moved (the prose always said `unfiled` keeps the finding deferred), and its `summary` zero-pass expectation from a zero record to a refusal, both by decision, not to pass.

## [1.91.255.0] - 2026-10-26

**Merge trains fill at 3 READY PRs or one hour after the first READY, and a train verdict's cost line no longer hides the trials it could not price.** On 2026-10-26 the 5-PR / 3-hour fill left READY PRs waiting most of a day, and `train verdict` printed `cost=$24.41` for a train whose slice report said `cost $32.92 known + 54 of 136 trial(s) cost unknown`. The slice report was right: 54 E2E trials had no cost attributed because their result records are named by a display label ("/benchmark workflow") while the case is named by its id (`benchmark-workflow`), so the per-case sum the train record carries was short by $8.51. Every train cost the coordinator reported until this fix was that undercounted verdict figure (about $24 per train against about $33 real).

### Changed
- **`.gstack/ship-policy.json`**: `train.max_size` 5 → 3 and `train.fill_hours` 3 → 1. `fillDue` already dispatches at either bound, whichever comes first; a fourth READY PR is `HELD:` for the next train. docs/ship-policy.md says so in the fill paragraph and its example block.

### Fixed
- **`scripts/lib/paid-report.ts`**: when a shard ran exactly one case (every case shard since W5a), its result records belong to that case even when they are named by a display label, so the trial's `cost_usd` is the record's and `cost_known` is no longer false; a failed trial in such a shard also takes its `failure_class`, `exit_reason` and `error` from that record (train-gate classes a red `infra` record INFRA instead of VERDICT) where it was a bare `assertion` with the JUnit message. No case's pass or fail changes. A multi-case shard whose records carry display labels keeps those trials cost-unknown rather than guessing which case paid. The train record's per-case `cost_usd` (scripts/train-gate.ts) and the slice report's headline now agree for case shards; the headline was never wrong.
- **`lib/ship-queue-train-verdict.ts`**: the `ATTEMPT:` line prints `cost=$<known> known + <n> of <m> case(s) cost unknown` when some but not every panel is priced, the bare `cost=$<sum>` only when every panel is priced, and no cost at all when none is (unchanged).

### Tests
- `test/gstack-ship-policy.test.ts` pins the live fill rule (3 PRs or one hour) and exercises `fillDue` with the live block at 59 and 60 minutes and at 3 PRs.
- `test/paid-report-census.test.ts`: a display-labelled record in the periodic fixture's `qa-fix-loop` case shard gives the trial `cost_usd: 1.23` with no `cost_known: false`, `verdict.costUsd` 1.23 and the headline `cost $1.23 known + 6 of 7 trial(s) cost unknown` (red before the fix: `cost_usd: 0, cost_known: false`); a failed display-labelled record gives the trial `failure_class: 'timeout'`, its exit reason, error and cost (red before the fix: `assertion` with the JUnit message); the two-case `skill-e2e-cso` shard keeps its display-labelled trial unknown while the id-named one is priced.
- `test/ship-queue-train-cost.test.ts`: a green train whose record has two unpriced panels prints `cost=$0.70 known + 2 of 3 case(s) cost unknown`; a fully priced record prints `cost=$1.50` alone (red before the fix: the bare `cost=$0.70`); every panel priced at zero prints `cost=$0.00`.
- `scripts/lib/windows-curation.ts` excludes `test/ship-queue-train-cost.test.ts` from the Windows subset like `test/ship-queue-train.test.ts`: both drive `bin/gstack-ship-queue` against the `#!/bin/sh` gh shim, which windows-latest cannot run.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, rubric, trial count, case kind or judge prompt changed. Cost attribution changes what a trial record reports, never whether a case passed.

## [1.91.254.0] - 2026-10-26

**Pregate ergonomics for a repository that is not gstack (Lane D, GSTA-112; plan harness-codify E4–E6; Captain issues 6, 11, 12).** Three Captains lost their first `/ship` pass to `PREGATE_NO_LANE` in a repo that had no `.gstack/pregate.json` yet (FOUN #292, harness-evals #81/#82); the non-downgradable `secrets` check refused 1,800 dummy per-trial tokens, 11-digit Actions run ids read as phone numbers and a public Firebase key every bundle rebuild re-adds (harness-evals #81/#83, GSTA-102, GSTA-106); a lane whose runner could not start read as the diff's failure and was waived by test name (truther #617); and pregate's logs under `os.tmpdir()` were shared between parallel runs and wiped by a Capy wake (gbrain 16).

### Added
- **No policy → warn plus a starter, never a hard `PREGATE_NO_LANE`** (`lib/pregate/starter.ts`, `lib/pregate/checks/lanes.ts`). When the base branch carries no `.gstack/pregate.json` and no user-owned policy exists, a touched file with no lane is a `warn` row under the new code `PREGATE_NO_POLICY`; the selected tests still run (a red lane is still `fail`, an unknown platform matrix is still a `requires-remote` obligation), and the table prints a starter policy drafted from the repository: the detected runner, the test directories, the CI lanes (naming a planner-computed matrix that needs `selection`), the JSON between `PREGATE_STARTER: begin` and `end` with a `dependencies` entry per unmapped touched file mapped to the tests nearest it or sharing its stem (never `[]`), and a `TODO` line per file nothing covers. `run` writes nothing; `gstack-pregate init` is the explicit write. Once any policy exists (base copy, user-owned file, or `--policy-from head`), an unmapped file is `PREGATE_NO_LANE` as before.
- **`allowlist` in `.gstack/pregate.json`** (`lib/pregate/allowlist.ts`, `lib/pregate/config.ts`, `lib/pregate/checks/secrets.ts`): `[{ finding, paths?, pattern?, reason }]`, where `finding` is a gstack-redact finding id or one of the categories `pii`, `internal`, `hygiene`, `legal`; `paths` are contained globs; `pattern` is a regex matched at the finding's position in the added line and ending at a token boundary; one scope is required and `reason` always is (64 entries at most). The `secrets` row says `N allowlisted (<ids>)`, lists each allowlisted finding with its entry and reason, and records the entries' digest as `inputs.allowlist`. **`env.value` (a credential-named environment variable's real value in the added lines, #3449) and the whole `secret` category can never be allowlisted:** validation refuses the entry (`PREGATE_CONFIG_INVALID` at `allowlist[i].finding`) and the matcher never consults the list for `env.value`, so a stale or hand-edited policy cannot silence it; the scanner's own `engine.*` refusals (an oversize input fails closed) are refused and kept the same way. A `pattern` entry that named a finding the scanner gave no position for is reported as not tested (the finding is kept) instead of silently inert. An unparsed scanner report keeps its exit-code verdict.
- **Environment failures reported apart from diff failures** (`lib/pregate/environment.ts`; new code `PREGATE_ENVIRONMENT` with the troubleshooting anchor `pregate-environment`). A runner or guard binary missing from PATH (exit 127, `command not found`, a spawn `ENOENT`, a tool `not on PATH`), a network error or a quota refusal before any test was counted, a full disk, an unverified runtime or gstack's own scanner not finishing is `incomplete` with `cause: "environment"` and `environment: { kind, evidence }` in `pregate.json`, an `environment: <kind> — <evidence>` table line and a fix; `PREGATE_LANE_FAILED`, `PREGATE_GUARD_FAILED` and `PREGATE_SECRETS` carry `cause: "diff"`. `environment.proof` records how the cause was established: `launch` (a spawn failure, a binary off PATH, a runtime or tool refusal; the fix ends "the diff is not at fault") or `output` (a rule matched the command's text before any test was counted, which the diff's own output could have written; the table line says `(inferred from output)` and the fix asks for confirmation on another machine or with `--remote`). The classifier is conservative: a local lane that exited non-zero is read from its output only when its runner reported no test summary and was not seen starting a test file; a counted failure is the diff's whatever its log says; exit 127 and `command not found` are `missing-binary` only when the command's own binary is off PATH, so a runner, guard or gate script the diff controls that exits 127 is the diff's; a remote gate is environment only when it printed no `PREGATE_REMOTE:` line and the cause sits in its first 40 lines, before any test output could stream; a runner killed by a signal, stalls and timeouts keep `PREGATE_INCOMPLETE` / `PREGATE_STALLED`. `gstack-pregate verify` prints `PREGATE_ENVIRONMENT: <n> check(s) blocked by the environment (<kinds>), not by the diff` when every incomplete check is environment-caused, naming any check inferred from output alone, and names the kinds beside `PREGATE_INCOMPLETE` otherwise, so a lane waives by cause and proof, never by test name.
- **One scratch directory per run under the state root** (`lib/pregate/run-scratch.ts`): `<state root>/projects/<slug>/pregate/runs/<run id>/` (0700; `--run <id>` names it, else `<UTC stamp>-<pid>-<4 hex>`) holds the secrets scan's added-line copies (deleted after the scan), `lanes/lanes.log`, `guards/<id>.log` and the remote gate's log and file list, never `os.tmpdir()`. `pregate.json` records it as `scratch`, the table prints `scratch: <dir>`, a taken `--run` name takes a numbered sibling (`<id>-2` … `-9`) rather than sharing the directory; runs older than 7 days under the same project are pruned when a new run starts; an unwritable state root falls back to a private per-run directory under `os.tmpdir()` and says so.

### Fixed
- **`literals` no longer floods on a common module stem or a one-digit value** (`lib/pregate/checks/literals.ts` `consumersOf`). A test file counted as a consumer of a changed constant when it merely contained the source file's stem as a bare word (`install`, `retry`), so `GSTACK_CAPY_WRAPPER=2 → 3` in `capy/skill/gstack/scripts/install.sh` flagged 575 test files (`PREGATE_LITERALS`; GSTA-114, #3475). The module now counts only as a path fragment (`/install.sh`, `/retry.js`, `/retry'`), and an old value shorter than two characters needs the constant's name in the file. The same edit now flags the 5 files that name `GSTACK_CAPY_WRAPPER`. Regression: `test/pregate-selection.test.ts` "consumersOf: a module stem is a path fragment…".

### Changed

## [1.91.253.0] - 2026-10-26

**`/captain` (also `/crew`): the crew operating model that keeps many agents merging into one base branch without turning it red, as a gstack skill with templates and a team guide.** Teams running a controller agent over worker threads had the model only in one crew's private notes. It now ships generic: one controller merges and lanes never merge; a READY block (full head SHA, base, CI counts, pregate, gate evidence, `SHIP_RECEIPT` at the pin, screen choice with justification, receipt path, logged flaky cases) is the only merge trigger, and a green PR page or a cheap test tier never is; merge trains (build, verdict, per-slot stamp on call, verify, merge with the expected head, verify again, prune), the red-train rules (in-run flaky rerun once, bisect on the red cases, exactly one unchanged rebuild, one infra re-dispatch), the tree rule, the backstop and the freeze, and the post-merge babysit; the digest shape (Needs you / New / In progress with ages); the three approval shapes (the per-thread record, the plan ask with before → after and a "do it" reply, the merge ask with captioned before/after images); and the daily flaky-fix pass (ledger format, the gate runs' flake records and the free suites' retries as sources, red-before-green fix PRs, one named infra rerun allowance, never thresholds, trials or kinds). Where crews that run this model disagree (squash or merge, lane or controller stamps, gate-ahead, the severe race, a gate run id in the READY) the skill ships both as options for the crew rules file. Every repo-specific name is a parameter (`REPO`, `BASE`, `REQUIRED_CHECKS`, `FULL_GATE_CHECK`, `MERGE_METHOD`, `STAMP_FILES`, `KNOWN_INFRA_FLAKES`).

### Added
- **`captain/SKILL.md.tmpl`**: the skill, tier 2, routed from the root router on "captain", "crew", a merge train, a slot call, a READY block or the crew digest; its own triggers add "validate this ready" and "flaky pass".
- **`captain/templates/`**: `CREW.md` (the 23 lane rules as one-line pointers into gstack's docs and skills, plus the crew's parameters and its standing-approval table), `AGENTS.md` (the controller's standing rules with the owner's dated words), `NOTES.md` (the append-only timestamped log), `DIGEST.md`, `flaky-ledger.md`, `report.md` (Outcome, PR, Needs, Cost, Lesson, Approvals), `READY.md` (the block, the optional lines, the refusal list), `slot-call.md`, `plan-ask.md`, `merge-ask.md` and `automation-flaky-pass.md` (the schedule, what it reads, what it starts).
- **`docs/captain.md`**: how a team sets up a Captain crew on Capy with gstack: the roles, the drive layout, the crew rules file, the READY contract, the lane's /ship sequence before READY, trains with the slot-2 recipe, approvals, the digest, the flaky pass, the owner's device, the lessons loop, and the setup steps; linked from the README docs table, `docs/skills.md`, `docs/capy-install.md` and the skill.
- **`test/captain-skill.test.ts`**: pins the contract the skill teaches, the template set, the generic wording (no crew codes, names or repository literals) and the registration points.

### Changed
- **`gstack-owner-brief render --captain`** closes "What we need from you" with the **do it** reply (every recommendation at full scope, the plan's follow-ons included, carried through with no further ask) and invites `rec` or `do it`; `capy/skill/gstack/captain.md` documents it as step 6 and points at the controller's side.
- `README.md` (power tools), `AGENTS.md`, `docs/skills.md`, `docs/PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md`, the root router and the doctor component table register the skill; `test/fixtures/context-budget.json` gains the `captain` ceiling and the router's, grown by its one new rule; `test/catalog-budget.test.ts`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/CONTRIBUTOR_REFERENCE.md` carry the catalog ceiling the new skill ratchets to; `gstack-autoplan answer` accepts `do it` as a `rec` alias.

## [1.91.252.0] - 2026-10-26

**`/retro` can now say whether the factory is getting better, and a new team has one page that takes it from zero to its first merged train on gstack + Capy.** `bin/gstack-factory-scorecard` reads one window (default 7 days) from GitHub through `gh` and prints a Markdown table plus a CSV: merged PRs (crew vs outside contributors), lead time (PR created → merged, and first READY comment → merged), gate runs green / red / cancelled with their known cost, cost per merge, the red-train rate, flaky events from the same two sources the daily flaky pass reads, issues opened vs closed, and releases cut. Each line carries its counting rule and what one of the best software factories would show on it; a line whose input cannot be read says `unavailable (<reason>)`, never 0. `docs/recommended-harness.md` is the adoption guide: install, the Captain and its Drive, the first train, the daily flaky pass, the weekly release, the scorecard with gstack's own numbers against the bar, what is Capy-specific, the options where two crews differ, and the known Capy limits as of 2026-10-26.

### Added
- **`bin/gstack-factory-scorecard`** (`lib/factory-scorecard.ts`): `--repo`, `--base`, `--since-days`, `--crew login,login` (else author association OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR), `--gate-workflow`, `--gate-event`, `--free-workflow`, `--train-prefix`, `--ready-marker`, `--pass-marker` and `--pass-cap` (review passes per PR: median, p90 and how many PRs sat at the cap, from the ship receipt's `"passes"` in the PR body or a `passes=N` / `REVIEW_PASSES: N` comment), `--max-artifact-runs`, `--out-dir`, `--csv`, `--json`, `--fixtures` (recorded gh responses, no network) and `--now`. `--repo` defaults to the origin remote's owner/name and is required without one; every run appends its rows to `trend.csv` in `--out-dir`. Gate cost comes from the run's `report-verdict-a*` artifact (`collector-outcomes.json` `.verdict.costUsd`), else the `**$N** rule/judge cost` or `cost=$N` line of the PR's verdict comment; flaky events from `flake-records-a*` (paid) and `flake-ledger-*` (free) artifacts. A READY comment posted after the merge is ignored, a PR's verdict-comment cost backs one gate run, and a run whose artifacts cannot be read is counted and named rather than scored 0. Read-only; exits 0 with the table even when an input is unavailable, 2 on bad usage.
- **`/retro` Step 7.5 (Factory scorecard, optional)**: the report format gains a **Factory scorecard** slot; the step runs the bin for the retro window when `gh` is authenticated and pastes the table, third column included, into the report.
- **`docs/recommended-harness.md`**, linked from the README docs table; `docs/standalone-binaries.md` lists the new CLI.

## [1.91.251.0] - 2026-10-26

**A free, deterministic design lint ships with gstack: `bin/gstack-design-lint` checks a page's HTML, CSS and components for the tells that make it read as machine-made, in under a second, and with `--render` measures what only a browser can.** Until now gstack's only mechanical design check was the opt-in impeccable engine most users never install, plus `gstack-design-craft`'s seventeen copy and ship-floor regexes; everything else in the Slop Gate was prose the model judged itself. The lint ports the roughly fifty-five machine-checkable gates of [Nutlope/hallmark](https://github.com/Nutlope/hallmark)'s `sloplint` (MIT; see NOTICE.md) into TypeScript under `lib/design-lint/`, rewritten in gstack's voice and mapped onto gstack's severity words. This release is the tool alone (Phase 1 of the hallmark absorption plan, approved by Garry on 2026-10-26); /design-html and /design-review start calling it in Phase 2, so no skill prose changes here.

### Added
- **`bin/gstack-design-lint <file-or-dir ...> [--render] [--url] [--scope page|component] [--job <job>] [--json] [--rules]`**: reads `.html`, `.css`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte` and `.astro` (Tailwind class strings included, `cn()`/`clsx()`/`cva()` calls too), links each page to the stylesheets it reaches through `<link>` and `@import`, resolves CSS variables, converts colours to OKLCH and computes contrast, and prints one line per finding: `LINT: <blocks|ask|polish|waived> <rule-id> <file>:<line> <evidence> | fix: <fix>`, then `LINT_SUMMARY: blocks=N ask=N waived=N polish=N render=<ran|skipped: reason>`. Exit 2 on blocks, 1 on an unanswered ask, 0 otherwise. `docs/design-lint.md` is the contract and lists every rule.
- **Three tiers in gstack's words, no fourth scale.** `blocks` (hallmark's Floor: contrast, focus rings, reduced motion, a card in a card, a purple-blue gradient, content hidden until JavaScript runs; never waivable), `ask` (hallmark's Reflex: three equal cards, Inter as the display, the centred-stack hero; waivable on the record) and `polish` (hallmark's Finish: straight quotes, a lonely last grid item; never blocks). Blocking and waived counts are never summed, so `blocks=0` is always a true sentence about the Floor. Three house rules hallmark holds at Floor stay at ask here: the eyebrow above a heading, the 80-word screen and the dash.
- **Waivers on the record.** `<!-- gstack-lint-disable <rule-id>: <reason> -->` (or the `/* */` and `//` comment forms; `impeccable-disable <rule>: <reason>` is an alias) answers an ask or polish finding when the reason is about this page: 24 characters or more, not boilerplate, not reused on another waiver, sharing a word with the page's own text. A waiver of a blocking rule is refused and the rule still fires; more than three waivers on one page is reported as a house style that belongs in DESIGN.md.
- **The render tier** (`--render`, or `--url` for a dev server) runs on the same engine `gstack-render` picks, Aside first and gstack's own headless browser otherwise, with nothing to install: the hero fits at 1280x800 (the headline's bottom and the first action; the lede and the visual are not measured), about 80 words per 900px window, contrast against the painted pixels, focus rings found by focusing every control, headings crowded against the section above, text painted under another element, horizontal scroll between 320 and 1920, wrapping button labels, a hero offering more than two actions, section gaps under 120px or all alike and more than nine sections, thin sections, dead bands, drawn illustrations, empty picture slots, counting marks and photographs covering more than a third of the page. Without a browser the summary says `render=skipped: <reason>` and the static tier still runs.
- `lib/aside-render.ts`: an eval step takes an optional viewport (`width`, `height`, `deviceScaleFactor`, `mobile`), set before the eval and cleared after it the way the screenshot step already does, and a spec's `file` may be an http(s) URL, opened as it is with no loopback server. Both engines take the size; `deviceScaleFactor` and `mobile` on an eval step reach Aside only (the browse daemon's `viewport` takes a size alone). Nothing else in the file changes.
- **The copy tier**: `gstack-design-craft`'s content-realism and ship-floor tells (placeholder names, lorem, buzzwords, round numbers, `[Needs proof]`, dead links, images without alt, the missing title, description, skip link and `aria-current`) report under the same contract and ids, so one command prints one list. `bin/gstack-design-craft` itself is unchanged until Phase 2 swaps the call.
- Fixtures under `test/fixtures/design-lint/` (hallmark's `slopped.html`, eyebrow and Tailwind pass/fail pairs and the waiver page, MIT-attributed, plus a clean page every rule family must leave alone); `licenses/MIT-hallmark.txt`; a NOTICE.md entry.

### Tests
- `test/design-lint.test.ts`: the parsers (nested CSS, tokens, var() fallbacks, colour spaces, JSX pseudo-HTML), the rule table against `docs/design-lint.md`, the output lines and exit codes, waiver acceptance and every refusal reason, the waiver fixture. One test per rule family (`test/design-lint-<family>.test.ts`) holds a negative control and a planted positive for every rule id. `test/design-lint-render.test.ts` drives the browse daemon when it is built and skips with a named reason otherwise. `test/design-lint-recorded.test.ts` lints the repository's recorded design slop page (the review eval's ground truth) and pins which rule answers each annotated issue, the same gate set hallmark's sloplint reports on the same files.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, budget, timeout, trial count or assertion was weakened. No template, catalog or eval changed. Gate edits in the diff: `test/fixtures/module-size-ratchet.json` registers the 27 new `lib/design-lint` modules under the existing 800-line cap, and `test/helpers/free-fixtures-data.ts` maps `test/fixtures/design-lint/**` to the design-lint test files; `lib/aside-render.ts` gains the viewport on eval steps and http(s) `file`, described above.

**Three free-tier fixtures stop racing themselves (GSTA-107 daily flaky pass).** Two tests polled for a result file's existence while its writer created it with a plain `writeFileSync`, so a poll between create and write read an empty file; a third copied a shared template repository with `fs.cpSync` and threw once inside the directory walk.

### Fixed
- **`browse/test/dotenv-isolation.test.ts`** (Free Tests 39902683183 and 40322888041, shard 2, "JSON Parse error: Unexpected EOF" at the `agent-env.json` read): the probe writes its result to a temp file and renames it into place, and `waitForFile` waits for content, not only for the file. A new test feeds the old race (an empty file filled 150 ms later) and runs the probe source itself.
- **`test/claude-code-runner.test.ts`** (Free Tests 39694715116, shard 13, `running(pid)` false at the timeout case): the descendant publishes `descendant.pid` by rename, and the test polls `publishedPid()`, a positive integer, instead of the file's existence, so an empty read can no longer become pid 0.
- **`test/cso-git-hardening.test.ts`** (Free Tests 40288142343, shard 17, `fs.cpSync` threw in `fixture()` with an empty message and passed on the serial retry): every fixture builds its own repository with Git instead of copying a shared template, with auto-maintenance off (`maintenance.auto=false`, `gc.auto=0`) so the detached `git maintenance run` a commit starts no longer touches `.git` while a test walks or removes it; the `beforeAll` still pays the cold macOS Git spawns once, on a throwaway repository. No timeout changed.

## [1.91.249.0] - 2026-10-26

**Five paid-case flakes from the 2026-10-26 train gates, repaired at their causes (GSTA-107 daily flaky pass).** The "ship-docsync family" was three distinct slips, not one shared cause: a mistyped `--help` path the detector refused although the usage had already been read, an undeclared refusal of gstack's own state directory as an artifact location, and a fixture that did not install the shared preamble a generated skill requires. tpa-present's consent question paraphrased "defer" as "wait for now", and qa-functional-webhook-fix ran the probe's `--help` bare before its first capture.

### Fixed
- **ship-docsync-store (gate 40323989742 slice 3):** a candidate `--help` typed at a wrong, non-existent path (exit 127) is ignored when the declared binary's `--help` ran anywhere in the transcript, before or after, since a help probe reads nothing the agent still has to recover (`test/helpers/docsync-observer.ts` `candidateNotFound`); snapshot and compare still need the declared retry after the slip, and a wrong path that exists, a failed declared run, or no declared run at all still fail.
- **ship-docsync-completion (gate 40290033102 slice 2):** the parent put its snapshot `--out`, saved section and report insert under `<home>/state`, gstack's own state directory (GSTACK_HOME), which the authority refuses but the fixture interface never named. The interface now says a private artifact lives directly under the fixture home or in a new directory there, and names every refused root: the repository, the installed skills, the Claude config dir, `<home>/state` and `<home>/remote.git` (`test/helpers/docsync-interface.ts`). The authority is unchanged.
- **docsync-spawned (PR #3434 screen 40269992077 slice 13):** `fixtureDocs` installs `<skill>/sections/preamble.md` beside the required sections when the generated skill has one, so a spawned child whose SKILL.md names the shared preamble as a required asset no longer blocks on its absence (`test/helpers/docsync-fixture.ts`). A generated skill without one installs exactly the files it did before.
- **tpa-present (gate 40290033102 slice 14):** the defer-option detector accepts "wait for now" and "hold off (on this) for now" as the option's own opening or sentence (`test/helpers/third-party-actions.ts` `offersDefer`); a drive option that waits while the user signs in, a "do not wait for now", or the phrase outside a lettered option still does not count.
- **qa-functional-webhook-fix (gate 40290033102 slice 9):** the fixture interface states that the evidence helper's `--help` is the only one it grants and that a bare `bun run probe` with `--help` or any argument outside a capture is a bypass (`test/helpers/qa-functional-eval.ts`); the grammar and the bypass detector are unchanged.

## [1.91.248.0] - 2026-10-26

**`$B` in direct mode no longer lets Chromium pick a proxy from the environment (#3440 item 8).** `BROWSE_PROXY_URL=direct` (and an unparseable `HTTPS_PROXY`) only stopped gstack from configuring a proxy. The daemon inherits the whole environment and the launch passed no proxy switch, so Chromium read `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY` or `ALL_PROXY` itself and every `goto` still went through that proxy while `$B` reported a direct connection. That made the BROWSER.md precedence list false and any certificate check on a proxied machine unreliable. Reproduced on Linux with Playwright 1.62.1: a logging CONNECT proxy in `HTTPS_PROXY` received `CONNECT <host>:443` with `BROWSE_PROXY_URL=direct` set.

### Fixed
- **`browse/src/browser-manager.ts`**: each of `BrowserManager`'s four Chromium launch sites (headless `launch`, the `BROWSE_EXTENSIONS_DIR` persistent context, `launchHeaded`, `handoff`) adds `--proxy-server=direct://` when no proxy is configured and `forcesDirect()` says Chromium would otherwise pick one browse did not resolve, from one `proxyLaunchArgs()`. A configured proxy was already explicit (Playwright passes it as `--proxy-server`), so the environment can no longer win silently in either mode. `--no-proxy-server` was measured and rejected: chrome-headless-shell, the default headless build, ignores it and still took `HTTPS_PROXY`; the full Chromium honors both switches, and `direct://` works on both. The cookie-import worker (`cookie-import-native-worker.ts`), which launches the user's own browser only to read its cookie store and never navigates, is unchanged.
- **`browse/src/proxy-config.ts`**: `forcesDirect(env, platform)` is true on Linux always, where the leak lives, and on macOS and Windows only with `BROWSE_PROXY_URL=direct`. Chromium there never read the proxy variables and follows the system proxy settings (PAC and WPAD included), so a user of GStack Browser.app behind a corporate proxy keeps that connectivity, and a PAC cannot be named through `BROWSE_PROXY_URL`. An explicit `direct` bypasses the system settings on every platform. A standard proxy variable without a scheme (curl-style `host:port` or `user:pass@host:port`) is now read as an `http://` proxy (port 80 when none is given). For `host:port` that is what Chromium's own environment reader took it as: before this change browse rejected it with a warning and Chromium on Linux read the variable anyway, so that session was proxied; with the launch now explicit, reading it the same way keeps those sessions on their proxy instead of sending them direct. `user:pass@host:port` follows curl's reading and is newly proxied: Chromium rejects any proxy spec that carries a userinfo (`net/base/proxy_string_util.cc`), so that session was direct before and now sends its credentials to the named proxy. On macOS and Windows the same value is now a configured proxy too, where it used to be ignored in favour of the system proxy settings, so a daemon started under the old warning meets the mismatch refusal once. Only the plain `[user:pass@]host[:port]` shape is read that way; a value with a scheme (including the slash-less `https:user:pass@host:port`, which the URL parser reads as `https://`), a `/`, `\`, `?`, `#`, `@` or whitespace anywhere else in the value, or a bare number goes to the URL parser as written, so a bare number such as `1234` keeps its diagnostic and a one-slash spelling such as `http:/host:3128` is read as the URL parser always read it (`http://host:3128/`). A proxy URL with a path other than a bare `/`, a query or a fragment (a literal `?` or `#` anywhere) is now refused for every source (`--proxy` included), because that is where a `DOMAIN\user` login or a `/` in a password lands after URL parsing and only the userinfo is redacted; percent-encode `/`, `?` and `#` in credentials for every scheme and `\` in `http://`/`https://` credentials (a `socks5://` userinfo keeps a backslash as written). This narrows the environment path: a credential-free value with a path, such as `http://proxy.corp:3128/pac`, used to be read with the path dropped and the session proxied; it now warns and goes direct like any other unusable standard-variable value, and `--proxy`/`BROWSE_PROXY_URL` refuse it. Credentials that are not valid percent-encoding (a literal `%`) are a proxy configuration error instead of a crash, for every source. For a standard variable each of these parse problems is a warning and a direct connection, like any other unusable value; a scheme-less value with credentials beside `BROWSE_PROXY_USER`/`BROWSE_PROXY_PASS` is now refused like its `http://` spelling, which has always been a hard error (that value used to warn and go direct because it did not parse). A value that does not parse even as `http://` (an unsupported scheme, a bad port, a missing host) still warns and connects directly; `--proxy` and `BROWSE_PROXY_URL` still require the scheme.
- **`browse/src/cli.ts`, `browse/src/server.ts`**: on macOS and Windows the explicit `direct` is part of the daemon config hash (`explicitDirect()`), is recorded in the daemon state as `proxyDirect` and is re-emitted on a crash auto-restart from the session's own flags, so a running daemon started on the system proxy is refused rather than reused by a session that opted out (the refusal names `BROWSE_PROXY_URL` and offers `browse stop` or unsetting it; a daemon started before this release meets that refusal once, and a daemon with no recorded config hash is refused like one started without `--proxy`; the mismatch refusal offers `BROWSE_PROXY_URL=direct` as a remedy only where it would match the running daemon, on Linux or against a daemon started with it, and otherwise says to unset the variable that differs). The unparseable-variable warning's hint now says that `BROWSE_PROXY_URL=direct` also bypasses the system proxy settings on macOS and Windows. On Linux the opt-out hashes like no proxy, as before, because every direct connection there already carries the switch.
- **`browse/src/server.ts`** logs the effective proxy mode each time the daemon starts, beside the existing `[proxy] using <url> from <source>` line: `[browse] [proxy] none: direct connection (--proxy-server=direct://; ignoring HTTPS_PROXY)` on Linux, naming each standard variable that was set and ignored; `(...; ignoring the system proxy settings)` for an explicit direct on macOS and Windows; and `[browse] [proxy] none: system proxy settings (Chromium's default on <platform>; BROWSE_PROXY_URL=direct connects directly)` when those platforms are left to the system.
