## [1.91.245.0] - 2026-10-26

**`gstack-ship-queue ready` counts CI the way GitHub's rollup does, and names the way through a CHANGELOG-only conflict.** A superseded run (gbrain saw a cancelled `contributor-gate` beside three later passes on the same head) made `ready` print `failed=1` where GitHub showed 0 failed, and a PR that conflicts with main on CHANGELOG alone had no documented route to green CI on its head.

### Fixed
- **`ready`'s `ci:` line** (`lib/ship-queue.ts`, new `latestRunPerName`) judges each check (one app's check name) by its latest run (newest `completed_at`, then highest id; a run still in progress is newest), so a cancelled or re-run earlier attempt no longer counts as a failure; two apps reporting the same name stay separate, a run without a name or without a readable `completed_at` counts on its own, and commit-status contexts are counted one each, as before.
- **`ready` prints a `ci-hint:` line on a conflicting PR** (`gh pr view` now also reads `mergeable`, `headRefName` and `isCrossRepository`): with no CI at the head it names the procedure (dispatch `free-tests.yml` and `windows-free-tests.yml` with `gh workflow run … --ref <branch>`, clear the pregate lanes with the run URLs, rerun `ready`); with green runs at the head it says the dispatched runs count; a head on a fork gets a hint that leaves the dispatch to the coordinator; a branch name outside `[\w./-]`, or starting with `-`, prints as `<branch>`. Every hint ends in `(advisory)`; nothing parses it. No hint without a conflict, or while the runs are red or pending.
- **Docs:** `docs/ship-policy.md` records that procedure under "Lane: report ready" (and that `--screen` is `QUEUE_SCREEN_STALE_REF` on such a PR for want of a merge ref, with advice that does not apply to a CHANGELOG-only conflict), rewords the `stamp-at-merge` row's `next:` description to the train wording `gstack-restamp` prints since #3439 (`commit and push only the stamp diff above (FILES), with no edit of your own`), and rewords the restamp `changelog` stage so `CHANGELOG_DUPLICATE_HEADING` is described as #3439 implements it: only a duplicate the PR introduces counts, measured against the base's CHANGELOG.

### Tests
- `test/gstack-ship-queue.test.ts`: two runs of one check name where the older is cancelled read green (either order), a newer failure reads red, a newer in-progress or queued run reads pending, equal `completed_at` falls back to the id, unnamed and undated runs stay separate, two apps with one name stay separate, a null conclusion reads red, and a commit status never collapses with a check run of the same name; a conflicting PR with no CI refuses with the dispatch hint, with green dispatched runs READYs with the "counts" hint, a fork head and an odd or dash-led branch name get the safe hint, and no hint appears without a conflict or while runs are red or pending.

## [1.91.244.0] - 2026-10-26

**A restamp PR no longer fails pregate for the manifests it stamps.** gbrain's `bun run release:restamp` rewrites its plugin manifests and VERSION; its base's `.gstack/pregate.json` declares no lane for them, and pregate reads policy from the base, so every such PR failed `lanes` with `PREGATE_NO_LANE` and could not fix itself (gbrain #7625, #7606).

### Fixed
- **`gstack-pregate` lanes**: a touched `*.json`, `*.plist`, `VERSION` or `VERSION.txt` file whose diff against the merge base changes nothing but its version values is waived as version-stamp-only, on its own line (`version-stamp-only (no lane needed): <files> — only version values changed against the merge base; a manifest whose other content changed still needs a lane`), with the per-file verdict under `--explain`. The rule is exact per kind (`lib/pregate/stamp-only.ts`): JSON objects of the same shape (same own keys in the same order, same array lengths, same leaf types) whose only changed leaf is the document's top-level `version`, a bare version on both sides, with the text differing on that line alone; plist `<string>` versions under `CFBundleShortVersionString` or `CFBundleVersion`; a VERSION file that is one bare version on both sides. Nothing nested qualifies (a dependency pin, a lockfile entry, a catalog), texts are compared byte for byte outside the stamped value (a line-ending change or a BOM is content), and a changed description, a new, removed or reordered key, a floor such as `minHostVersion` or `MinimumOSVersion`, a change the parser would erase, an invalid-UTF-8 or over-1-MiB file, a mode change or symlink, an added, deleted or renamed manifest, a file under a test, fixture, golden, `.gstack/` or workflow tree, or any other file kind is not a stamp and keeps its `PREGATE_NO_LANE`. It applies only after the import graph, the declarations, the regen registry and both empty lanes found nothing, so a manifest a test reads still selects that test. `docs/pregate.md` and the `PREGATE_NO_LANE` troubleshooting entry state the rule.

## [1.91.243.0] - 2026-10-26

**The launch environment reaches every gstack command and child through a sourceable file, and nothing in a skill fence may print the environment (GSTA-104).** During GSTA-96's unattended /ship on #3425 (2026-10-26), the Step 14.5 docs-audit child was told to export the `GSTACK_LAUNCH` assignments and re-typed them as `export $(...)`. The substitution came back empty, the shell ran a bare `export`, and the values of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and UBICLOUD_API_KEY landed in its tool output. The line itself carries no secret (PATH, GSTACK_SESSION_KIND, GSTACK_STATE_ROOT, GSTACK_EPHEMERAL, GSTACK_CAPY, GSTACK_INSTALL_VERDICT); the hazard was re-typing it. Now the installer writes the assignments as a file callers source, every fence that hands the launch environment to a child says so in one line, a free ratchet keeps environment dumps out of every skill fence and shell helper, and the redaction engine refuses a credential value from the writer's own environment, whatever its shape.

### Added
- **`GSTACK_LAUNCH_FILE: <verdict file without .json>.env`** after the `GSTACK_LAUNCH` and `GSTACK_LAUNCH_PATH` lines of every passing `bin/gstack-capy-install` run, `--check` included . The file is part of the ok verdict: a passing run that cannot write it exits 1 with `gstack: fail launch-file — could not write the launch file <path>; fix: … (LAUNCH_FILE_UNWRITABLE)`, and a failing run announces no launch file and removes the one an earlier passing run left beside the verdict it rewrites (a profile check that keeps a fuller ok verdict leaves that verdict's file; an unwritable directory keeps both the old file and the old verdict), so no caller is left with only the line and the re-typing path. The file holds the same assignments as `export` statements (the PATH prepend is idempotent), is written atomically with mode 0600 beside the install verdict under the state root, and is applied with `. <file>` at the start of the shell that runs a gstack command. A caller hands a child the path, never the values.
- **`env.value` (HIGH) in `lib/redact-engine.ts`**: the value of every `*_KEY`, `*_TOKEN`, `*_SECRET`, `*_PASSWORD`, `*_PASSWD`, `*_PASS`, `*_PAT`, `*_APIKEY` or `*_PWD` variable in the scanning process's environment (any case; eight characters or more after trimming, not a placeholder; names carrying a `PUBLIC` word and gstack's own `GSTACK_BRAIN_LOCK_TOKEN` are exempt, and there is no path exemption: a path-valued `SSL_KEY` that must appear in a text goes through `gstack-redact --allowlist` or the pre-push hook's `.gstack-redact-allowlist`, and for the writers that take no allowlist the variable is set empty for that one command) is a finding wherever it appears in the scanned text, so a leaked value cannot reach a PR body (`gstack-post`), a ship receipt, a report, an approval row or a Drive mirror through any writer that scans with the engine. The value is matched in the same normalized form as the text, so a value NFKC rewrites still finds its leaked bytes; when one value is a prefix of another, the longer value is redacted whole; the finding's preview never shows a byte of the value. `redactFindingSpans` removes it on the machine-egress path; `ScanOptions.processEnv` names the environment (`{}` scans without one). `test/redact-env-value.test.ts`.
- **`test/launch-env-echo-ratchet.test.ts`**: every generated SKILL.md and section file, their templates, `autoplan/DRIVER.md`, the Capy skill, every shell helper under `bin/`, `setup` and the `scripts/*.sh` install scripts carry no `export $(...)`, `export \`...\`` or unquoted `export $VAR`, no `env` or `printenv` (flags alone included), and no bare `set`, `export`, `declare -x`, `typeset -x`, `declare -p` or `typeset -p` in any command segment of a fence (`set | grep '^NAME_'` stays allowed: the anchored filter bounds what prints). `test/fixtures/launch-env-echo/` holds the negative controls the scanner must trip on.

### Changed
- **`ship/sections/documentation.md.tmpl`** (Step 14.5 subagent prompt), **`document-release/SKILL.md.tmpl`** (spawned note), **`autoplan/DRIVER.md.tmpl`** and the runtime `capy-asks` block of **`bin/gstack-skill-start`** (every workflow started with `GSTACK_CAPY=1`, /review and /qa included) each say in one line: apply the launch environment with `. <GSTACK_LAUNCH_FILE>`; never `export $(...)`, `env`, `printenv` or a bare `set` in a tool fence, because a bare `export` prints every variable, credentials included. /review and /qa dispatch no child that runs a gstack command, so their SKILL.md files, whose sizes are pinned, are unchanged. Nearby prose in the Step 14.5 section was tightened so /ship's union stays under its parity cap (313,279 of 313,281 bytes).
- **`capy/skill/gstack/SKILL.md`** (the source of the Drive skill) and **`docs/capy-install.md`** describe the launch file and name the incident; the Drive copy needs the owner's recopy to say the same.
- **`scripts/lib/shard-engine.ts`** `createShardSandbox` and the test preload (`test-setup.ts`, so a direct `bun test <file>` matches the lanes) drop `GSTACK_SESSION_KIND`, `GSTACK_CAPY`, `GSTACK_EPHEMERAL` and `GSTACK_INSTALL_VERDICT` from every test's environment, so a run started from a shell that sourced the launch file no longer hands the product-under-test children an unattended Capy session they never set up (GSTA-99's finding); each fixture sets its own session kind. `GSTACK_STATE_ROOT` and PATH are kept.

### Gate integrity
- One test budget changed: `test/setup-gbrain-remote-caller.test.ts`'s late-completion case gives its second attempt 2s (was 250ms) with a 20s test timeout (was 10s) after it failed 4 of 4 on windows-latest once the new files repacked the Windows shards (run 40263984171). No other gate, threshold, budget, timeout, trial count or case kind changed. The redaction scan only gained findings, minus the framework-public and non-secret exemptions named above. Size pins are unchanged: the edited skills are under the limit.

## [1.91.242.0] - 2026-10-26

**`gstack-context-bill` now bills a real install.** On `~/.claude/skills` it reported "2 skills, ~134 tok" always-on, because setup installs each skill as a real directory whose `SKILL.md` and `sections/` are symlinks into the gstack checkout, and the walker only counted regular files. The tool built to answer the token-cost complaint gave a falsely tiny answer on the layout users actually have. On a fresh install it now reports 58 skills, ~6.8K tokens always-on, and 3.6 MB on disk (it was 37 KB across 2 skills). Billing the checkout itself is unchanged (66 skills, ~7.2K tokens).

### Fixed
- **`lib/context-bill.ts`**: `findSkillDirs`, `walkMd` and the foreign-file check follow symlinked files and directories. Every path the bill reports, and every file `--exact` keys on, stays the lexical path under the root you passed. A link to a directory that contains the tree being billed or the skill being walked (`..`, `/`, `$HOME`) is never followed, so a link cannot climb out of the root into its parent or your home directory, even from a symlinked skill that lives elsewhere. The markdown walk expands each real directory once and counts each real file once per skill, under the first path reached in sorted order, which is how a skill loads it: loops end, links that fan out into each other cannot multiply the walk, and a tree with more than 200,000 entries is refused with an error instead of being cut short. `--exact` walks and sends only what the bill walks (the same per-skill walks and fences, so a link no skill bills is never walked), each real file once, measures frontmatter only for the `SKILL.md` files the bill prices it for, and prices every link to it with that one measurement. It sends only files inside the tree, inside the gstack checkout that the tree's `gstack/` entry links to (a git checkout with `VERSION`, `setup` and a `SKILL.md` named `gstack`; `bin/dev-setup`'s `.claude/skills/gstack -> <repo>` counts), or inside gstack's render folder `$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/render` (where setup renders the `SKILL.md` files that gbrain, `--claude-model` and per-install renders link to; trusted only when `render` is a real directory, not a link). Each file is judged by its realpath, so a link out of one of those folders is refused too; anything else a symlink reaches (a skill's `notes -> ~/Documents`, say) is not sent, its directory is named in the notice, the files are listed, and they are estimated offline. The notice also says how many sent files come from the checkout and how many from the render folder. A bill in which `--exact` had to estimate any item (a refused file, or one that changed after it was measured) says so: `tokenSource` starts with `mixed:` and names the count, `tokenEstimateErrorPct` keeps the estimate's 40% band, and the text output says the counts are mixed instead of measured. A measurement is reused only for a file that still has the realpath, inode, size and mtime it was measured with, so a link retargeted or a file rewritten after the measurement (during `--diff`, say) is estimated and counted as estimated instead of inheriting the old count. Billed paths are matched to their measurement one link at a time, so a second skill sharing a link chain deeper than the kernel's limit is still priced from the one measurement. Files are opened without blocking, so a file swapped for a FIFO is refused instead of hanging the run. An empty `.md` file and a `SKILL.md` without frontmatter are measured as zero tokens without a request, and a whitespace-only `.md` file is not sent and is estimated (so the bill says mixed), because `count_tokens` rejects content with no non-whitespace text: a blank file used to drop every measurement with a 400, and an empty one turned a fully measured bill into a mixed one. When every file `--exact` could send is blank, nothing is sent, no receipt is written, and the notice says so (and whether other files were refused). The sending notice is printed after the files are read, just before the receipt, and counts exactly the files sent. A state root that is missing, unreadable or not a directory just means there is no render folder to trust; the bill still runs. Each file is read through the realpath its walk recorded and only while it is still that same file, so a link retargeted or a file swapped for a link mid-run is refused rather than sent. A link named `*.md` counts only when its target is a `.md` file, so `--exact` never sends a non-markdown file through a markdown-named link. `walkMd` skips a child repo checkout (the `gstack/` link beside the installed skills), as `findSkillDirs` already did, so `--exact` does not send the whole checkout. The walk and skill discovery read each directory through its realpath, so a chain of links deeper than the kernel's 40-link limit no longer drops files or skills silently. Skill discovery has the same 200,000-entry cap as the walk. A container skill skips only nested directories whose `SKILL.md` is a file, as discovery does, so a `sub/` whose `SKILL.md` is a directory is billed to the container instead of to nobody. The root container also skips a nested skill that a directory link reaches at any depth (discovery already bills it), so `refs/alias -> ../sub` no longer counts `sub`'s files a third time in TOTAL. `--exact` on a path that does not exist now stops with `No such tree` before any request, including `--diff` with one missing tree (it used to send its one-character envelope probe first, and `--diff` sent the whole first tree), and its notice counts the same list of files it then sends. An existing tree with no skills sends nothing and writes no egress receipt, a tree whose skills have no markdown file to send says the offline estimate was used, and a tree whose every billed file was refused says so. `--help` now says which `.md` files `--exact` sends and that others are named and estimated.

### Tests
- `test/context-bill.test.ts`: an installed-layout fixture (a checkout outside the skills root, real skill directories with symlinked `SKILL.md` and `sections/`, and a `gstack/` link to the checkout) bills both skills with the target's exact frontmatter, `SKILL.md` and section bytes, and keeps every walked path under the root. Negative controls: a dangling `SKILL.md` link and a `SKILL.md` link to a directory are not skills. A second fixture holds a self link, a parent link that reaches a skill outside the root, a loop back into the skill and a link up to the temp root; only the one real skill and its own files are billed. Further cases cover a loop to a directory below the walk root, a root whose name starts with `..`, a symlinked `agents.md` (with a dangling link and a directory of a foreign-file name as controls), `--exact` on the installed layout (every billed file measured; nothing behind `gstack/` or a `.md`-named link to a non-markdown file is sent), a 12-level fan-out of links that reaches one file by 2^12 paths (walked once, where a walker that expands every link would return all 4,096), two skills linking one checkout file and directory (each real file sent once, both skills priced from it), a symlinked skill outside the root with a link up to the root's parent, the `--exact` notice's count of files from the gstack checkout, a skill whose `SKILL.md` another skill's walk reaches first under another name (its frontmatter still measured), a container skill whose nested skill links to the container's own files (both skills still bill them), `--exact` on a missing tree and `--diff --exact` with a missing second tree (named, with no request sent), a symlinked skill with a link up to its real parent (the files there are not billed, so not sent, and no billed file is keyed through that link), an existing tree with no skills (no request, no receipt), a skill whose `SKILL.md` links to a non-markdown file (no request, no receipt, and a line saying the estimate was used), a reference file with frontmatter (no frontmatter request for it), an install whose skill also links `notes` to a documents folder (the checkout files are sent; the documents file is refused, named, listed and estimated), a `gstack/` entry that is not a gstack checkout (a plain folder, a bare `.git` folder, another project's repo, or a gstack-shaped folder without `.git`: nothing behind it counts as the checkout), a `bin/dev-setup` tree inside the gstack repo (its skill files are sent), refused files in nested and sibling folders (each folder named once), every billed file refused (said so), a link retargeted, a file replaced by a link or a hard link, or a parent folder swapped during `--diff --exact` (never sent; a swapped file stops the run), a 50-deep chain of links (every file walked, billed and, under `--exact`, measured), a skill 45 directory links deep (discovered), skill discovery past its entry cap (refused), a `sub/` whose `SKILL.md` is a directory (billed to the container), a tree with no skills under `--exact` (no estimate line), a root container with a `refs/alias -> ../sub` link and a link to an outside folder holding a skill (neither nested skill billed to the container), a file swapped for a FIFO after the walk (refused within the subprocess timeout, where it used to hang), two skills sharing a 50-deep link chain (both priced from one measurement, nothing estimated), a `SKILL.md` link retargeted to a bigger file and a reference rewritten in place after measurement (both estimated and counted as such), a bill with a refused skill (`mixed:` in `--json` and in text), a file replaced by one of the same size and mtime (estimated), a skill without frontmatter plus an empty reference under a `count_tokens` stand-in that rejects empty content (still fully measured), a render folder that is itself a link (not trusted), a tree whose only file is empty, alone and beside a refused link (no request, no receipt, and a notice naming which case it is), a whitespace-only reference under a stand-in that rejects it (not sent, estimated, the bill labelled mixed, and the notice counting only the file sent), the render folder found through `GSTACK_STATE_ROOT` with no state root passed in, a state root that is a file (the bill still runs, measured), a git checkout inside a skill or linked from one (not billed; this case passes on main and fails when the walk's `.git` check is removed), and a render install (its `SKILL.md` and sections sent from `$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/render`, a link from there to a documents file refused and listed). The installed-layout and escape fixtures fail on main (the first finds no skills, the second bills the outside skill), the missing-tree case fails on main (one request sent), and each later case failed on the commit before its fix, except the hard-link and parent-swap cases, which pin the identity check added with the realpath reads (they fail when that check is removed).

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, budget, timeout, trial count, case kind or assertion changed. The bill of this repo's own tree, which the context-budget ratchet reads, has the same skills, bytes and rounded token figures as on main. Four raw `totalMdTokens` values in `--json` differ in the last floating-point digit, because each skill's files are now summed in sorted order.

## [1.91.241.0] - 2026-10-26

**The weekly OSV scan on main is green again, so the weekly release cut can run.** The 2026-10-26 scan ([run 40288353843](https://github.com/garrytan/gstack/actions/runs/40288353843), #3462) found 14 fixable vulnerabilities in six packages across both lockfiles, and the release workflow skips any main commit with a red check run. Every one is bumped to its fixed release; no application code changed, because gstack imports none of these packages directly (the MCP SDK and zod arrive through `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`, body-parser through its express, fast-uri through ajv, ip-address through socks and express-rate-limit, dompurify through mermaid).

### Fixed
- **dompurify 3.4.16 → 3.4.17 in `lib/diagram-render`** (GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7, CVSS 9.2; GHSA-mrv2-3pqr-j5jr; GHSA-c6gr-qvv4-5v3f). The override moves and the committed bundle is rebuilt with Bun 1.4.2 (two builds, one sha256 `c2d37f9f…`), so the shipped page runs the fixed sanitizer instead of a bundled copy of the old one. Mermaid, excalidraw and React pins are unchanged.
- **@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.31.0 → 1.32.0** (GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw, GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453, GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq, GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw), **fast-uri 3.1.8 → 3.1.9** (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h) and **ip-address 10.7.3 → 10.7.4** (GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5) through the existing `overrides` pins.
- **zod 4.5.4 → 4.6.7** (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5, fixed in 4.6.6) and **body-parser 2.3.0 → 2.4.0** (GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828) through the lockfile alone; both sit inside their consumers' ranges, so no override was added. body-parser 2.4.0 brings a nested qs 6.16.1.

### Changed
- **`lib/diagram-render/scripts/build.ts`** empties the one `VITE_APP_FIREBASE_CONFIG` literal that `@excalidraw/excalidraw`'s npm bundle carries (excalidraw.com's public Firebase client key, which nothing in the package reads and the offline render page never uses). The build fails if the literal is not matched exactly once or any `AIza…` key survives, so an excalidraw bump that changes its shape cannot put the key back silently. Without this, every rebuild of the committed bundle failed the pre-gate secret scan.

### Tests
- `test/diagram-render-drift.test.ts` asserts the bundle's DOMPurify is the `package.json` override and no other version, and that it carries no Google API key; its path constants are repo-relative segment runs so the pre-gate's import graph selects it for the bundle, `BUILD_INFO.json` and the build script.
- `test/deps-smoke.test.ts` refuses `ip-address` below 10.7.4 and checks every resolved version of the six packages against its OSV-fixed floor in both lockfiles (all six fail on main's lockfiles). OSV-Scanner 2.3.8 with the workflow's own arguments (`--config=.osv-scanner.toml --include-git-root --recursive ./`) reports no issues on this tree; the katex ignore is the only filtered advisory.

## [1.91.240.0] - 2026-10-26

**Proactive skill suggestions default to the four core skills.** `proactive` now takes `core` (the default: only /office-hours, /review, /qa and /ship auto-invoke when a request matches), `all` (any matching skill, the old behavior) or `off`. `true` and `false` keep working as `all` and `off`. The sentiment research (GSTA-93) found auto-invocation of every skill is what makes gstack collide with other skill packs; the four core skills are where the praise is, so they keep the nudge. Garry, 2026-10-25: "do it".

### Changed
- **`bin/gstack-config`**: `proactive` defaults to `core`; `set proactive` accepts `core`, `all`, `off`, `true` and `false` in any case, stores the YAML yes/no family (`yes`/`on`/`1`, `no`/`none`/`0`/`disabled`/`never`) as `all`/`off`, and warns on anything else, storing `core`. The config header documents the three values.
- **`SKILL.md.tmpl`** (the router): three branches, `off`, `core` and `all`; under `core` only the four core routing rules auto-invoke, the browser step and the Failures branches name `/browse` or `/investigate` for the user to type, and a skill the user names is always invoked. The opt-out line writes `off`, and `all` and `core` have their own lines.
- **Every skill's preamble** (`scripts/resolvers/preamble/generate-upgrade-check.ts`): the steady-state rule names the four core skills under `core`, scopes the setting to unasked suggestions, carves out only the skills the user names or the running skill invokes itself ("Skills the user names or this one invokes run", so `/ship` dispatching `/document-release` is not a suggestion, while an in-skill offer to run another skill still counts as one under `off`), reads only `core`, `all` and `off` because `gstack-skill-start` now reports the legacy spellings as those, and is exactly as long as before, so the 89 size pins in `test/fixtures/skill-md-size-allowlist.json` are unchanged.
- **`bin/gstack-skill-start`**: the one-time prompt offers "Keep the core four (recommended)", "Suggest every matching skill" and "Turn it off", writing `core`, `all` or `off`. `scripts/question-registry.ts` lists the same three options.
- **`bin/gstack-skill-start`**: the `PROACTIVE:` STATUS fallback when `gstack-config` is missing is `core`, not `true` (found by /ship's coverage audit, red at the first head); a stored value gstack does not know reads as `core`, the legacy `true`/`false` and the yes/no family read as `all`/`off`, and a hand-edited value is unquoted, lowercased and stripped of a trailing comment first, so STATUS only ever says `core`, `all` or `off` and a typed opt-out never fails open (found by /ship's red team: `proactive: "off"` read as `core`); the first-run and first-loop tips name only core skills and stay quiet under `off`; the one-time offer to add `## Skill routing` to the project's CLAUDE.md is not made under `off` (found by /ship's red team: the routing rules are the auto-invocation the user turned off); a user who stored `off` before the one-time proactive prompt is not asked (the prompt marker is written before STATUS reports `PROACTIVE_PROMPTED`).
- **`office-hours/sections/design-and-handoff.md.tmpl`**: the next-review handoff takes the recommend-only path under `off` as well as the legacy `false` (found by /ship's review); under `core` it still offers the review, because a step inside an invoked skill is part of that skill, which the router now says in so many words.

### Added
- **`docs/proactive.md`**: the three values, who each is for, the legacy spellings, the commands, and the approved fallback (`off` if collisions continue). Linked from docs/skills.md.

### Tests
- `test/proactive-config.test.ts`: the default in get, list and defaults; the five accepted values stored verbatim, an upper-case `OFF` stored as `off`, the yes/no family stored as `all`/`off`; the warning and `core` fallback on an unknown value (negative control: `maybe`).
- `test/proactive-core-set.test.ts`: every surface (config header and default, router template and render, preamble, one-time prompt and registry, docs, office-hours gate, tips) names the same four core skills and the same three values, with negative controls (no non-core skill in the core block, `true` no longer "the default", no `set proactive false` left).
- `test/proactive-skill-start.test.ts` runs the script: STATUS is `core` when unset or unknown, the stored value otherwise, `all`/`off` for the legacy spellings and for a quoted, upper-case or commented hand edit; the missing-`gstack-config` fallback equals the config default (regression test: failed at the first head); the CLAUDE.md routing offer and the first-run and first-loop tips fire under `core` and not under `off` (marker unwritten).
- Known gap, follow-up #3446: under `core`, the `## Skill routing` section gstack offers for a project's CLAUDE.md, and the "Proactively suggest" sentences in non-core skill descriptions (full catalog mode), still route every skill; docs/proactive.md says so.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, budget, timeout, trial count or case kind changed. Size pins unchanged (the preamble is byte-for-byte the same length).

## [1.91.239.0] - 2026-10-26

**BROWSER.md now says that gstack's own browser still trusts the compromised eMudhra intermediates, and how to check (#3338).** Chrome blocked eight eMudhra intermediate CAs by CRLSet on 2026-10-17, the day their key compromise was reported, and scheduled the removal of their root, emSign ECC Root CA - G3, from the Chrome Root Store for 2026-10-27. gstack's default headless browser gets neither: it launches with Playwright's `--disable-component-update`, so it receives no CRLSet updates, and the root store built into the bundled Chromium still trusts the root. On 2026-10-24, `$B goto https://dv-g3b-emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/` loaded the test page on gstack's pinned Playwright 1.62.1 (Chromium 151.0.7922.34), and Chrome for Testing builds from 158.0.8115.0 fail it with `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID`, so the Playwright bump waits for a release that bundles one of those builds.

### Changed
- **`BROWSER.md`**: a new "TLS trust: the bundled Chromium's root store" section, at the end of the security stack, gives the warning, the plan (move to the first Playwright release whose Chromium is 158.0.8115.0 or later; until then, no signed-in work in this engine on an untrusted network) and the check: on a network that does not inspect TLS, after `$B stop` and once a known-good HTTPS site loads in headless mode, only `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID` on the test host means a build is fixed. Environment-dependent caveats (proxy variables, profiles, custom builds, headed CRLSet timing) are tracked in #3440. The table of contents, the fallback-engine introduction and the `cookie-import-browser` and `handoff` command rows link to the section. Aside is unaffected, because it is your own browser with its own updates.

### For contributors
- The edits above the cookie workflow excerpt change no line count, so the `setup-browser-cookies/SKILL.md workflow` judge input is byte-identical (prompt SHA-256 `c851e635…`, 12,805 bytes, before and after).

## [1.91.238.0] - 2026-10-26

**Five /ship frictions the unattended lanes hit (GSTA-102).** Each fix is one commit.

### Fixed
- **`gstack-gate-diff <base>` in a clone with no local `<base>` branch.** Before, `gstack-gate-diff main` in a checkout that cloned only its feature branch printed `GATE_ERROR=no_base ref=main fix=git fetch origin main`, and that fix did not help: the tool only tried the local branch, and in a single-branch clone a bare `git fetch origin main` updates FETCH_HEAD alone. Now `lib/gate-diff/git.ts` resolves the base to its remote-tracking branch (`origin/main`, origin first, then the other remotes) when no local branch exists, says so once on stderr, and the merge-base is the same commit. When the remote-tracking branch is missing too, the fix line fetches into it explicitly: `git fetch origin +main:refs/remotes/origin/main` (with `--unshallow` on a shallow clone), which works in every clone shape. `test/gate-diff-cli.test.ts` adds a single-branch clone fixture with no local `main` and no `origin/main`: it asserts the error, runs the printed fix verbatim, and expects the next run to list the fixture's RH-1 hunk; two more clones cover a second remote that carries the branch when origin does not, and an upstream-only clone of a master-default repository whose default base (no argument) now comes from the same remote list as the fix line. The refspec is forced (`+main:refs/remotes/origin/main`) so the line also repairs a tracking ref that exists but shares no history with HEAD.
- **`gstack-post` no longer flags the repository's own release versions as public IPs.** A four-part version is byte-for-byte a dotted quad, so "(1.91.191.0)" in a PR body raised `pii.ip_public` (MEDIUM) and stopped an unattended docs audit that cannot confirm a MEDIUM finding. The engine's version exemption only reads the declaration right before the span (`"version": "`, `## [`), so prose that merely names a release got no help. Now `lib/gstack-post.ts` reads the root `VERSION` value and every version in a root `CHANGELOG.md` release heading (`## [1.2.3.4]`, `## v1.2.3.4`, through the same `parseChangelog` gstack-restamp uses) and passes those exact strings to the scan's allowlist. Verdict: this narrows one detector by the repo's own release set, and nothing else. The allowlist is exact-string and context-free, so a released quad is exempt wherever it appears in the text, `host: 1.91.191.0` included; the set is the repo's own releases and nothing wider. `8.8.8.8` and `203.0.113.7` in prose, a quad the repo never released (`1.128.1.0`), and the same text outside a repository or in a repo whose VERSION is three-part all still need confirmation; `test/gstack-post.test.ts` carries those controls beside the four benign bodies (`(1.91.191.0)`, `v1.91.226.0`, a bare `1.91.191.0`, `release 1.91.190.0`) against a synthetic CHANGELOG in which `1.91.192.0` is not a release. The same post path also stops reading a ship receipt's all-digit tree hash (`tree=704992822996`) and an 11-digit GitHub Actions run id in prose or link text (`run 19368712345`, `[run 19368712345](…/actions/runs/19368712345)`) as `pii.phone.e164`: only the exact tokens in those positions are allowlisted, and `+14155551234`, a bare 11-digit number and a 10-digit number after `run` still need confirmation (GSTA-94 hit this on #3424).
- **`gstack-evidence` records the test count of gstack's shard runner and of the remote pregate lane.** `bun run test:free` / `test:ubicloud` run quiet shards that forward bun's `Ran N tests` line without its ` N pass` counts, so the bun parser read every full-suite run as `tests_ran: 0` and /ship's Step 16 saw a zero-run suite (GSTA-94 on #3424); the remote lane prints `PREGATE_REMOTE: tree=… tests=9660 failed=0` (a lane row under `lanes:` in the pregate table) and `requires-remote: … cleared by remote-gate tree=… tests=9660`, which no parser knew, so it was `tests_ran: unknown` and the ship receipt and the Review Readiness Dashboard never carried the number. Now a bun terminal line with no counts block above it is not a bun summary (bun always prints ` 0 pass` / ` 0 fail`, even for an all-skip run, which still grades ZERO-RUN), the shard runner's per-shard `[test:free] PASS — N tests` epilogues are summed for the last run in the output (a files-from run's `FILES-FROM RESULT: … tests=N` is the same sum; a run with a `FAIL —` or `FLAKY-PASS —` epilogue and no such total has lost a shard's count and is recorded as unknown, not a partial sum), and when the shard runner spoke its verdict stands for the whole tail (the tail is the stdout tail then the stderr tail, so a line's position cannot order bun's stderr counts block against the runner's stdout epilogues; a focused `bun test` run before the suite in the same command no longer records its count, or ZERO-RUN, for the 10k-test run that followed), and the remote lane's two lines are parsed as whole lines like every other runner pattern (a prefixed or quoted echo does not count; the later line wins when both appear); a paid-only selection's `tests=0` is ZERO-RUN, not a pass. Honest limit: the shard runner and the remote gate print only bun's terminal totals, which include skipped tests, so for those two the number is tests ran with skips included, not executed (the shard runner refuses a shard whose bun summary counts fewer files than planned, but a shard whose files all loaded and executed nothing still passes with that total). The exit code is still never changed by the parse. `test/evidence.test.ts` runs the wrapper over `test/fixtures/evidence/pregate-remote-failed.out`, the stdout of a real `gstack-pregate --stage tests --remote` run captured under gstack-evidence on 2026-10-26 (9658 tests, 1 failed, recorded as `tests_ran=9658` with `exit=1`, never FRESH), over a cleared lane's table (`tests_ran=9660`, FRESH), over the receipt line alone, over the two lines with differing counts in both orders, and over `test/fixtures/evidence/shard-runner-files-from.out`, the remote gate's own shard-runner stream for this branch (275 files, 16 shards, 10138 tests: the epilogue sum equals the `FILES-FROM RESULT` total, with and without that final line, and a forwarded `Ran N tests` line on stderr no longer zeroes it).
- **`gstack-restamp` refuses only the CHANGELOG duplicates the PR introduces.** `CHANGELOG_DUPLICATE_HEADING` compared the branch's headings with themselves, so a base branch whose released history already heads one version twice (gbrain's `master` carries two `## [0.38.0.0]` sections, and its own check requires every one of them to stay) could never be stamped. The check now takes the base branch's CHANGELOG, read at `origin/<base>` and at the commit the branch's own lines are counted from (its fork point, or the predecessor's head in a gate-ahead stamp), the larger count per heading winning: a heading the base carries N times may appear N times on the PR, and only a further copy is refused, with a message that says how many the base has. When a reading is unavailable (the PR adds the CHANGELOG itself) the stage detail and the refusal name it. A duplicate the PR adds, on a clean base or beside an inherited one, is still refused with nothing written. Tests: a fixture whose `main` heads `1.2.2.0` twice stamps and keeps both copies, and still does after `main` collapsed the copies behind the PR's back; a PR that adds a third copy, one that adds the first duplicate on a clean base, and one whose new CHANGELOG on a base without one heads a version twice, are refused. `docs/troubleshooting.md` says which duplicates count.
- **`gstack-restamp --next` under a train no longer asks the lane to edit the CHANGELOG.** Its `next:` line told every stamp to "write the CHANGELOG entry text"; a lane that obeyed on #3422 added a release summary under the new heading, the train's verify refused the head (the CHANGELOG must equal the base's plus the PR's own entry re-headed) and the queue froze. Under `queue_mode stamp-at-merge` the line now says to commit and push only the stamp diff with no edit of the lane's own; the claim-at-open wording is unchanged, since that bump still writes its entry at /ship's CHANGELOG step. Test: the stamp-at-merge fixture's output carries no instruction to edit the CHANGELOG by hand, and the claim-at-open fixture still does.

## [1.91.237.0] - 2026-10-26

**An unstamped PR can change a release output again (GSTA-96 on #3434).** Regenerating `agents-digest/gstack-AGENTS.md` after a generator change made the Version Gate classify the head as stamped (the digest is in `release_outputs`) and demand base + bump, while changing only `scripts/gen-agents-digest.ts` failed `test/agents-digest.test.ts`'s freshness check, so a digest rewording could not land before its slot.

### Fixed
- **Version Gate under a train policy** (`lib/version-gate-train.ts`, `scripts/compare-pr-version.ts`): a changed `release_outputs` file no longer counts as a stamp when it is byte for byte what the policy's `release_tool` generates at the head's merge base's `VERSION` (the head's own, since `VERSION` is unchanged on this path; the base tip may have stamped since, and CREW rule 14 says not to merge it); the gate runs the head's tool in a throwaway worktree with that `VERSION` (the changed outputs removed first, a bare environment with `GSTACK_RESTAMP_VERSION` and `GSTACK_RESTAMP_STAGING=1` and none of the gate's tokens, no `node_modules` link, a 120 s limit enforced with SIGKILL so a tool that ignores TERM cannot hold the gate open, output read from a file, first 4 KB, so a lingering child cannot either) and compares byte for byte. `VERSION` and `package.json` version changes still classify the head as stamped, as does an output that differs (hand-edited, generated at a bumped version, or never written by the tool) or a policy with no `release_tool`; a tool that exits non-zero, is killed or cannot be staged is an error with the reason, never a pass; the staging worktree is removed and pruned on every path. `version-gate.yml` checks the head out with `persist-credentials: false`, since the head's tool now runs inside the gate. The freshness test stays strict and a stamp commit still changes only the stamp files, since the slot's restamp regenerates the output. `docs/ship-policy.md` states the rule under "Lane: report ready".

### Tests
- `test/compare-pr-version.test.ts`: a generator change with its regenerated output at the merge base VERSION passes as unstamped (red without the fix), and stays unstamped after main stamps again; a tool whose background child outlives it does not hold the gate open, nor does one that traps TERM (`regeneratedAtBase` is exported for that test); a hand-edited output, an output generated at the bumped version, an output the tool never writes, a VERSION bump without the output, a failing release tool and a policy without `release_tool` all still refuse; the tool sees no `GH_TOKEN`; no worktree is left behind.

## [1.91.236.0] - 2026-10-26

**The merge queue now refuses a PR that never ran /ship.** Garry, 2026-10-25: "we should really be using the gstack ship skill before merging PRs." `gstack-ship-queue ready` printed `SHIP_RECEIPT: none in the PR body` as information and returned ok, so every PR in the pool was READY'd without a /ship run. The receipt /ship writes into the PR body is now a precondition at `ready`, `train build` and `verify --train`, with no flag around it.

### Changed
- **`gstack-ship-queue ready`** refuses with `QUEUE_RECEIPT_MISSING` when the PR body has no valid ```gstack-ship-receipt``` block and with `QUEUE_RECEIPT_STALE` when the receipt's `head` is not the head being READY'd (or its `pr` is another PR). The re-READY after a slot's stamp push accepts the receipt written for the pin when HEAD is the pin plus stamp files, or (from slot 2 on) the pin merged with main plus stamp files. The informational `SHIP_RECEIPT:` line still prints in the block, and it is one line whatever the receipt's strings contain (control characters are collapsed, so a crafted `base` cannot add a forged `MERGE_CONDITION:` line to `verify --train`'s output).
- **`gstack-ship-queue ready --screen` refuses a stale merge ref** with the new `QUEUE_SCREEN_STALE_REF` (GSTA-95 on #3431): GitHub stops recomputing `refs/pull/<n>/merge` while a PR conflicts with the base (a CHANGELOG-only conflict after a stamp counts), so a screen dispatched there planned 0 cases, reported success and `ready` printed `SCREEN_DISPATCH:` as if a screen ran. `ready` now compares the merge ref's head parent with the PR head before dispatching (a missing merge ref carries the same code), never adopts a finished screen that planned no cases (a superseded run skips plan-slices and uploads no `paid-plan` artifact; a manifest with nothing planned counts the same), and `train build` prints `SCREEN: #<n> run <id> planned no cases …; counted as not-run` and seats that slot unscreened (a plan it cannot read keeps the slot screened and prints `… counted as screened, unverified`).
- **`gstack-ship-queue train build`** refuses a pin whose PR has no current receipt with the same codes, naming the PR, before any write, push or dispatch, `--dry-run` included. **`verify --train`** refuses the slot the same way before `MERGE_CONDITION`, and accepts a receipt written for the slot's pinned head when the current head is its stamp commit (the stamp changes only stamp files, or merges main into the pin from slot 2 on), since no /ship runs on a stamp.
- **`gstack-ship-receipt result`** (new) is /ship's terminal step: it binds the posted receipt to HEAD, writes `<state root>/ship/runs/<utc>-<head12>/{ship-run.json,ship-receipt.md}` (a /ship record, not a `run` v1 manifest: `gstack-artifact validate` does not apply) and prints `GSTACK_RESULT: skill=ship status=complete run=<dir>`, `status=refused run=-` with the receipt code, or `status=incomplete run=-` when gh cannot read the PR, so a parent's merge check reads `ship-run.json` instead of parsing the PR body. The ship skill's new Step 22 runs it after the pr-body and handoff sections.
- **Unattended /ship may update an existing PR's body.** `gstack-skill-start`'s unattended block and `UNATTENDED_SHIP:` line, the ship skill's Step 18 and `docs/unattended.md` now say: when an open PR for the branch exists and HEAD is its pushed head, Step 18 takes the pr-body section's existing-PR path (body with the receipt first, and title); it never runs `pr-create` and never pushes a commit; anything else takes the handoff section. Before this the block said the receipt lived only in `.gstack/tmp/ship-receipt.md` while rule 22 and `ready` read it from the PR body.
- **`INSTALL_UNVERIFIED` with no verdict names the directory to install from.** An installer run from the skill's own folder records a verdict for no project, so /ship launched from the project found none and the fix said only "run the installer on this machine" (GSTA-85). Both twins (`lib/install-verdict.ts`, `bin/gstack-install-verdict.sh`) now say `run … scripts/install.sh --for ship from <project>: the verdict is keyed by the project directory the installer runs in`.
- **Docs:** `docs/ship-policy.md#ship-before-ready` (the lane runs /ship before every READY and after every push; the stamp keeps the pin's receipt; the receipt is a process gate, not an authenticity check), the three codes in `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `docs/unattended.md` (/ship now prints the result line), and the ship skill's pr-body section says what refuses without a receipt.
- **Gate edit (size budgets):** `test/helpers/carve-guards.ts` raises ship's `maxSkeletonBytes` 81,000 → 81,600 and `maxSizeRatio` 1.6690 → 1.6740 for Step 22 and the Step 18 routing, offset in part by tightening Steps 14, 16, 18 and 20 prose (measured skeleton 81,535, union 314,027; the 2026-10-14 tightening had left 2 bytes of headroom). No threshold, trial count or case kind changed.

### Tests
- `test/ship-queue-train.test.ts`: READY, train build (dry run and live) and verify --train refuse a missing, invalid, other-head and other-PR receipt and admit the current one; the pinned-head receipt admits a stamp commit; verify refuses `QUEUE_PROOF_MISSING` when gh cannot read the PR; `--screen` refuses a lagging or missing merge ref and never follows a 0-case screen. The train fixture's `refs/pull/<n>/merge` is now a real merge commit (`mergeRefCommit`), as GitHub keeps it. `test/gstack-ship-queue.test.ts`: `ready` at a stamp commit (slot 1, and slot 2 with main merged in) accepts the pin's receipt; a bare merge of main with no stamp on top, an empty commit over the merge, or an edit on the pin side under the slot-2 stamp, is `QUEUE_RECEIPT_STALE`. `gstack-ship-receipt result --pr <n>` refuses `QUEUE_RECEIPT_STALE` when HEAD is not the PR's pushed head and prints `status=incomplete` when gh returns no head or the run record cannot be written; `ready --screen` names a failed `ls-remote` or fetch of the merge ref instead of blaming a conflict. Both install-verdict twins tell an unreadable verdict file from a missing one. `test/auq-error-fallback-hook.test.ts`: the unattended directive names the same `GSTACK_RESULT` writers as docs/unattended.md and `gstack-skill-start` (GSTA-91). `test/gstack-ship-receipt.test.ts`: the `bindReceipt` head-matching table (12-character floor, other PR, one-line `SHIP_RECEIPT:`), `result --body` refusals, `--head`, a non-git cwd and gh failures. The train fixture's `openPr` now writes a receipt for the head it opens (`shipped: false` leaves the body empty). `test/install-verdict.test.ts` pins the GSTA-85 fix in both twins; `test/gstack-skill-start.test.ts` pins the new unattended /ship block.

## [1.91.235.0] - 2026-10-26

## [1.91.234.0] - 2026-10-26

**Weekly tagged releases, and a `stable` channel that team-mode auto-update follows by default.** Main kept stamping a version per merge, a dozen a day, with no tag or release anywhere, and `./setup --team` installs moved to every one of them within the hour. Now a Monday-morning workflow tags the newest green commit on main as `v<VERSION>`, publishes a GitHub Release from the CHANGELOG headlines and fast-forwards a `stable` branch to it; team installs follow `stable` and move once a week (plus hotfixes), contributors keep following main, and one config key switches either way. Nothing about per-merge stamping or the merge train changed (docs/releases.md).

### Added
- **`.github/workflows/weekly-release.yml`**, **`scripts/release-cut.ts`**: every Monday at 14:00 UTC, or by `workflow_dispatch` (`dry_run`, default true for a manual run; `ref` for a hotfix), the newest first-parent commit on main whose `free-tests` and `main-backstop` check runs succeeded, with every check run finished and none red and no active freeze in `refs/notes/gstack-trains`, is tagged `v<VERSION>`, released with one headline per CHANGELOG version since the previous release (capped at 60 KB), and becomes `refs/heads/stable`. Stable only moves forward along main; a candidate behind it, a tag naming another commit, or a frozen queue is `REFUSED`. A cut that stopped half-way (tag and `stable` pushed, release not created) is finished by the next run. A dry run prints the plan and the exact commands and changes nothing (nothing green is exit 0 for a dry run, with every skip named); a pull request that touches the workflow or the script runs that dry run against main as a read-only job. The cut job runs only from `refs/heads/main`, takes `ref` as a full 40-hex SHA, and has `contents: write` and `checks: read` only; both rulesets cover `refs/heads/main` alone, so the token can push the tag and `stable`.
- **`.github/workflows/evals-main-backstop.yml`**, **`scripts/train-backstop.ts`**: the backstop's verdict is published on the commit as the `main-backstop` check run from a code-free `checks: write` job (`--outputs` records the action): success for `covered` and `gated`, neutral for `superseded`, `deferred` and `inert`, failure for `frozen` and `failed`. The run's own conclusion is exit 0 for a superseded push (main moved past it before it was gated), so reading the run would have called a never-gated tree green; the release reads the check run instead.
- **`bin/gstack-update-channel.sh`**: resolves the channel (`gstack_update_channel`: `update_channel` `auto` is `stable` when `team_mode` is true, else `main`; `GSTACK_UPDATE_CHANNEL` overrides), and as a command (`--fetch-ref`) fetches the channel ref and prints `origin/stable` or `origin/main` for the /gstack-upgrade skill.
- **`bin/gstack-config`**: new key `update_channel` (`auto` | `stable` | `main`), validated on `set`, in the header, `list` and `defaults`.
- **`docs/releases.md`**: what a release is, what green means, the channels and how to switch, hotfixes, dry runs and every outcome line.

### Changed
- **`bin/gstack-session-update`**: on the stable channel it fetches `+refs/heads/stable:refs/remotes/origin/stable` (team installs are single-branch clones) and fast-forwards to it, logging `CHANNEL stable target=<sha>`. Before the first release exists it follows main (`CHANNEL_FALLBACK stable->main`). An install already past the release stays put (`CHANNEL stable ahead_of_release`, then `UP_TO_DATE`): a depth-1 clone cannot relate the two commits, so the VERSIONs decide. The main channel's fetch, target and log lines are unchanged.
- **`bin/gstack-update-check`**: reads `<channel>/VERSION`, resolves the SHA with `ls-remote refs/heads/<channel>` and compares against it; the cache identity carries `#stable` so a channel switch never replays the other channel's outcome. With no `stable` on origin yet it follows main for that check, as the session updater and `gstack-upgrade` do, instead of caching `CHECK_FAILED` from a 404 until the first cut.
- **`bin/gstack-upgrade`**: fetches and fast-forwards to `stable` on that channel (`gstack-upgrade: channel stable ...` on stderr), follows the default branch with a note when origin has no `stable` yet (an `ls-remote` that fails is a fetch failure, not an empty answer), and treats a release whose VERSION is not higher than the installed one as current instead of diverged in a shallow clone. `--check` output lines are unchanged.
- **`gstack-upgrade/SKILL.md.tmpl`**: Step 4 resolves `UPSTREAM_REF` through the helper and uses it for the Bun-floor check, the fast-forward, the unpushed-commit gate and the reset fallback instead of a literal `origin/main`; the fallback block requires the carried `UPSTREAM_REF` (`:?`) instead of defaulting to `origin/main` in a fresh shell, and a team install already past the release stops with `AHEAD_OF_STABLE` instead of `FF_REFUSED` and an offer to reset backwards. The helper's `--fetch-ref` keeps `origin/stable` when the fetch fails for any reason other than a missing release, so a network blink never moves a team install to main; its unused `gstack_update_channel_ref` is gone.
- **README** Step 2 (team mode) says team mode follows `stable` and how to follow every merge instead.

### Tests
- `test/release-cut.test.ts`: on a real bare origin with a fake `gh`, the newest green first-parent commit wins and every skip is named (pending or neutral `main-backstop`, red check run, missing or running `free-tests`, no `main-backstop` check run, an unrelated check run still going); an active freeze refuses and a cleared one does not; a cut creates the annotated tag, `stable` and the release with `--verify-tag` and the headline in the notes; re-running is `NOTHING_NEW`; a cut whose `gh release create` failed is finished by the next run with notes against the release before it; the CLI exits 0 on a dry run with nothing green and 1 on the real cut; a hotfix `--ref` promotes a later main commit with a compare link; stable never moves backwards; a side-branch ref and a clashing tag are refused; a thousand-version span stays under the notes cap.
- `test/update-channel.test.ts`: the resolution matrix (team mode × key × env override); the session-start hook on a depth-1 team install moves to stable (B) not main (C), follows main on `update_channel=main`, falls back to main with no stable on origin, and stays put when already past the release with nothing pending; `gstack-upgrade --check` and the upgrade follow stable then main after the key flips, say when no release exists, and call a depth-1 install past the release current; `gstack-update-check` on stable stays silent while main is ahead, asks `ls-remote` for `refs/heads/stable`, carries the channel in its cache identity, and follows main when origin has no stable yet; `--fetch-ref` keeps `origin/stable` when origin is unreachable.
- `test/weekly-release-workflow.test.ts`: the workflow's triggers, concurrency, the cut job's main-only guard, permissions and 40-hex `ref` check, and the read-only pull-request dry run. `test/evals-train-workflow.test.ts`, `test/train-backstop.test.ts`: the `backstop-check` job's action-to-conclusion map, its code-free `checks: write` split, and the CLI's `--outputs` line.
- `test/upgrade-template-pins.test.ts`, `test/gstack-upgrade-fresh-shell.test.ts`: the pinned fast-forward, unpushed-commit gate and reset markers name `"$UPSTREAM_REF"` instead of `origin/main`; the ordering invariants are unchanged.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, budget, timeout, trial count, case kind or assertion changed. The release workflow reads check runs and the trains notes ref; it dispatches nothing and runs no tests or evals. The backstop gates exactly as before; it additionally publishes its verdict as a check run.

## [1.91.233.0] - 2026-10-26

**/plan-tune's inferred profile no longer pins at 1.0 after a few reviews, and it now records how many answers moved each dimension.** This closes the last two parts of #2623. One /plan-eng-review produces about five answers, and every answer added its full delta, so eight sessions of "fix now" took `architecture_care` to 0.998, as uninformative as the 0.5 it replaced. Now each UTC day moves a dimension at most as far as one strong answer, and eight days of the same answers read 0.808. The profile JSON (`--profile`) also records `contributing_events` per dimension, so a dimension with no evidence reads 0 there instead of a bare 0.5; /plan-tune's display and `--check-mismatch` don't read it yet (#3436).

### Fixed
- **`bin/gstack-developer-profile`**: `--derive` sums each UTC day's deltas per dimension (by the row's `ts`) and clamps the sum to the largest single delta in the signal map (±0.06 today). Answers within a day net out before the clamp. Only an ISO 8601 date or date-time `ts` counts as dated, and a time without a zone is read as UTC; every other row shares one undated bucket, so a junk timestamp can't escape the bound. `diversity.days_span` counts the same UTC days. The bound ignores `session_id` on purpose: the PostToolUse hook and the agent log different ids for one review, and an unsubstituted `SESSION_ID` placeholder would merge every review into one bound or leave each answer unbounded. Several reviews on one day count as one. `--trace` uses the same accumulation, so it lists every contributing answer, each clamped day ("day 2026-04-01: +0.250 capped to +0.060") and a `TOTAL` line whose value matches `--derive`.
- **`bin/gstack-developer-profile`**: a logged choice named after an `Object.prototype` member, such as `constructor`, or a log line that parses to a non-object such as `null`, no longer makes every later `--derive` and `--trace` fail; signal lookups use own properties only. `--trace` replaces control characters in the logged fields it prints, so a logged `ts` can't forge a `TOTAL` line.

### Added
- **`inferred.contributing_events`**: per dimension, the number of logged answers that moved it (an answer that writes two deltas to one dimension counts once). Ported from #2625 by @v639dragoon, with co-author credit. #2625's autonomy signal from `followed_recommendation` stays parked, as decided in its Oct 8 review.

### Docs
- `docs/designs/PLAN_TUNING_V0.md` documents `signal_events`, `contributing_events` and the per-day bound in the profile schema, including why the bound ignores `session_id`.
- `TODOS.md`: the #2623 entry now covers only its remaining Gate 1 work, the `{skill}-{slug}` hinted fallback, tracked as #3442.

### Tests
- `test/gstack-developer-profile.test.ts`: `contributing_events` counts unique rows when one answer writes two dimensions, and is all zero for an answer that matches no signal. The bound equals the signal map's largest delta. Five answers on one day move a dimension by exactly the bound in both directions, whether they carry one `session_id`, five different ones, the literal `SESSION_ID` placeholder, or one review logged by both the hook and the agent. The day is the UTC day of `ts` even when the machine's zone is west of UTC, and a `ts` without a zone, `T`- or space-separated, is read as UTC. `--trace` prints the clamped days and a total that matches `--derive`, and replaces control characters. A `constructor` choice, a `null` line and array-valued `question_id` or `user_choice` rows are ignored. Rows whose `ts` is not ISO 8601 (`TS`, `junk 1`, a number) share one undated bucket and add no days to `days_span`. Negative controls: the same answers on separate days, a second day after a capped first day, and an answer pair that nets out are not clamped. The original positive tests fail against the old bin; the day-bound, `constructor` and control-character tests fail against the per-session version; a one-sided clamp fails the bound tests, and local-day bucketing fails the UTC tests.
- The test helper `logQuestion` sets `GSTACK_QUESTION_LOG_NO_DERIVE=1`, so the background derive can't race a test's own `--derive` (from #2625).

### Gate integrity
- No test expectation, threshold, budget, timeout, trial count or case kind changed.

## [1.91.231.0] - 2026-10-26

**A fresh install is about 520 MB smaller: `./setup` installs production dependencies only.** Setup ran `bun install` without `--production`, so every user also got the test and eval toolchain from `devDependencies`, mostly the Claude Agent SDK's native binaries (both the glibc and musl builds on Linux, ~440 MB). Measured on a clean Ubuntu 24.04 container with a cold Bun cache (4 vCPU, two runs each): `node_modules` goes from 1,094 MB to 572 MB, the checkout from 1.74 GB to 1.22 GB, and the whole install with Chromium from 2.42 GB to 1.90 GB. `./setup` took 24.6 s and 20.0 s before, 21.1 s and 18.9 s after.

### Changed
- **`setup`**: every dependency install (before the build, the Codex render and each host render) goes through one `install_runtime_deps` function: `bun install --production --frozen-lockfile`. Bun treats `--production` as frozen, so when `bun.lock` is behind `package.json` (a fork or a local edit) it refreshes the lockfile with `bun install --lockfile-only` and installs production-only again. **`bin/gstack-browser-ensure`** installs the same way when `node_modules` is missing, and its failure line suggests the production install rather than a full `bun install`.
- **`package.json`**: `@anthropic-ai/sdk` (loaded by `gstack-distill-free-text`, /plan-tune's dream cycle) and `xterm` and `xterm-addon-fit` (copied into the browser extension by `bun run build`) move to `dependencies`, because a user install runs them. The Claude Agent SDK, TypeScript, Prettier and `@types/bun` stay dev-only.
- **Contributors and CI keep the full install.** `./setup` treats a checkout that already has the dev toolchain (`node_modules/typescript`) as a contributor's and runs the full `bun install --frozen-lockfile` there, so dev packages keep following `bun.lock` after a pull (a production install would report "no changes" and leave them at old versions). `bin/dev-setup` now always runs `bun install` (it skipped it when `node_modules` existed, which would have left a checkout first set up by `./setup` without the dev toolchain). CI workflows already run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` themselves. CONTRIBUTING.md says which command installs what.

### If you already have gstack installed
- An existing install keeps its dev dependencies and keeps getting the full install, because it already has the dev toolchain. To get the space back: `cd ~/.claude/skills/gstack && rm -rf node_modules && bun install --production --frozen-lockfile && rm -rf "$(bun pm cache)"/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk*`. The last step matters: Bun hardlinks `node_modules` into its global cache, so the Agent SDK's binaries stay on disk until their cache entries go. Don't do this in a checkout you develop gstack in.

### Tests
- `test/setup-production-deps.test.ts`: `install_runtime_deps`, sliced out of `setup` and run against a recording `bun` that models Bun's frozen `--production`, passes `--production` on the frozen-lockfile call, refreshes a stale lockfile before retrying, and stops setup when the refresh fails. A checkout with the dev toolchain gets the full frozen install, and a failed full install stops setup too. A walk of `bun.lock`'s production closure (with required-peer and optional-peer controls) proves no production dependency brings in `typescript`, the marker setup checks. The real-Bun rows run with `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `BUN_CONFIG_*` isolated, so a developer's global `.bunfig.toml` cannot change them. Run with the real Bun on local `file:` packages: a fresh install leaves out devDependencies, a later production install keeps the ones a full install added, and a stale lockfile is refreshed while the install stays production-only. No other line in `setup` calls `bun install` (the pre-change line is the negative control). `bin/dev-setup`'s install block, run over an existing `node_modules`, still calls plain `bun install`. A scan of every shipped file (`bin`, `lib`, `browse/src`, `design/src`, `make-pdf/src`, `hosts`, `extension`, the resolvers, and the scripts `setup` and the build call by path) finds no import or `require` of a package outside `dependencies`. Modules the shipped code reaches by relative import (gen-skill-docs' `scripts/` helpers, and the `test/helpers/providers` modules `gstack-model-benchmark` loads) are scanned too. Negative controls: a planted Agent SDK import is caught, including one split over several lines and a re-export; a type-only import is not; and moving `@anthropic-ai/sdk` back to dev flags `gstack-distill-free-text`. The packages `bun run build` copies out of `node_modules` are production dependencies.
- `test/gstack-browser-ensure.test.ts`: with `node_modules` missing, the preflight runs the frozen production install, refreshes a stale lockfile before retrying, and ends a failed install in `BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE` with a production-install fix line.
- The install fixtures' stub `bun` (`test/helpers/install-fixture.ts`, `test/helpers/claude-overlay-fixture.ts`, `test/team-mode.test.ts`) now matches `install --production --frozen-lockfile`. The team-mode stub fails on any other argv; the two helper stubs hand other commands to the real `bun`, so for them the new argv is a match, not a regression check.

### Gate integrity
- No threshold, budget, timeout, trial count, case kind or assertion was weakened. The four stub patterns (in three files) changed to the new argv only.

## [1.91.230.0] - 2026-10-26

### Changed
- **The archetype the user picks on the /design-shotgun board now reaches /design-html.** Captions name the archetype id (`classic-hero`, `long-form-story`, `minimal-conversion`, `comparison`). On approval, approved.json also gets the chosen `archetype` and its `sections` outline, added with the Edit tool so no free text reaches a shell command. /design-html reads both in Case A, and the craft section uses them as given instead of choosing again or asking.
- **Accepted craft exceptions persist.** /design-html's finalized.json records each accepted `CRAFT_CHECK` finding in `craft_exceptions` (`id`, `count`, `reason`) and carries forward earlier ones. A later run passes that file with `--accepted`, so a finding the user already accepted is reported as accepted instead of flagged again. A higher count is still flagged as a new issue.

### Added
- **`gstack-design-craft --accepted <finalized.json>`**: a finding whose id an exception covers, at no more than the accepted count, prints `CRAFT_ACCEPTED: <id> <count> <reason>` and doesn't fail the check. `CRAFT_RESULT` adds the accepted count. Exit codes: 0 when only accepted findings remain, 1 for unaccepted ones, and 2 for an unknown argument or a missing, unreadable or malformed exceptions file. A bad exceptions file still gets the full check with nothing accepted, after a warning, so a broken record can't switch the craft check off. A finalized.json with no `craft_exceptions` field, written before this change, means no exceptions.

### Tests
- `design-html-slop-gate` is now selected by changes to `lib/design-craft.ts` and `bin/gstack-design-craft` (`test/helpers/touchfiles-data.ts`), which it already exercised but did not list.
- `test/design-craft.test.ts` also covers accepted exceptions: count coverage and overflow, duplicate ids carried forward (the highest count wins), a bad exceptions file still checked in full, the finalized.json block in design-html/SKILL.md parsed by the same reader the CLI uses, rejected malformed lists, CLI exit codes with `--accepted`, and the archetype handoff contract (the same four ids in /design-shotgun and the craft section, the approved.json step, Case A and the craft section's no-re-ask rule).
